title.zh: 卷一百五十九 列傳第一百〇九: 衛次公 鄭絪 韋處厚 崔群 路隨
title.en: Volume 159 Biographies 109: Wei Cigong, Zheng Yin, Wei Chuhou, CuiQin, Lu Sui
title.raw: 卷一百五十九 列傳第一百〇九: 衛次公 鄭絪 韋處厚 崔群 路隨 Volume 159 Biographies 109: Wei Cigong, Zheng Yin, Wei Chuhou, CuiQin, Lu Sui

sentences.zh: 衛次公，字從周，河東人。

translations.literal: Wei Cigong, courtesy name Congzhou, was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cigong, whose courtesy name was Congzhou, came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 器韻和雅，弱冠舉進士。

translations.literal: His capacity and bearing were harmonious and refined; at the age of twenty he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful in both talent and demeanor, he obtained his jinshi degree while still in his early twenties.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎潘炎目為國器，擢居上第。

translations.literal: Pan Yan, Vice Minister of Rites, regarded him as a treasure of the state and raised him to the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yan, Vice Minister of Rites, saw in him a man who would serve the realm well and placed him at the head of the examinations.

sentences.zh: 參選調禮部侍郎盧翰嘉其才，補崇文館校書郎，改渭南尉。

translations.literal: When he entered the selection process, Lu Han, Vice Minister of Rites, praised his talent; he was appointed Collator of the Chongwen Hall and later transferred to be Magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: During the examination and appointment process, Vice Minister of Rites Lu Han commended his abilities; he was made collator at the Chongwen Hall and subsequently assigned as magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 次公善鼓琴，京兆尹李齊運使其子交歡，意欲次公授之琴。

translations.literal: Cigong was skilled at playing the zither; Li Qiyun, Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, had his son cultivate friendship with him, intending that Cigong teach him the zither.
translations.idiomatic: Cigong was an accomplished zither player; Metropolitan Governor Li Qiyun of Jingzhao had his son befriend him, hoping Cigong would pass his skill on to the boy.

sentences.zh: 次公拒之，由是終身未嘗操弦。

translations.literal: Cigong refused; from this he never touched the strings for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Cigong declined, and for the rest of his days he never played the zither again.

sentences.zh: 嚴震之鎮興元，辟為從事，授監察，轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Yan Zhen governed Xingyuan, he recruited him as an aide; he was granted the office of Supervisory Censor and later transferred to Palace Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen, as military governor of Xingyuan, took him on as a staff officer; he received appointment as a supervisory censor and was soon promoted to palace investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年，征為左補闕，尋兼翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Zhenyuan era, he was summoned to serve as Left Remonstrator and soon additionally appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 8 he was recalled to court as Left Remonstrator and before long was also made a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月，德宗升遐，時東宮疾恙方甚，倉卒召學士鄭絪等至金鑾殿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year, Emperor Dezong ascended to the remote heights; at that time the Eastern Palace's illness was very severe, and in haste the academicians Zheng Yin and others were summoned to the Jinluan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhenyuan 21, Emperor Dezong died; the crown prince was gravely ill, and Zheng Yin and the other Hanlin academicians were hurriedly summoned to the Jinluan Hall.

sentences.zh: 中人或云：「內中商量，所立未定。

translations.literal: A eunuch said: "Within the palace there has been discussion, and who is to be established has not been decided."
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch remarked, "Inside the palace they are still deliberating—the succession has not been settled."

sentences.zh: 」眾人未對。

translations.literal: The assembly did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: No one in the group answered.

sentences.zh: 次公遽言曰：「皇太子雖有疾，地居冢嫡，內外系心。

translations.literal: Cigong abruptly spoke, saying: "Although the Crown Prince has an illness, in position he is the eldest legitimate son, and within and without all hearts depend on him."
translations.idiomatic: Cigong spoke up at once: "The crown prince may be ill, but as the legitimate eldest heir he remains the focus of hope throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 必不得已，當立廣陵王。

translations.literal: If it absolutely cannot be avoided, then the Prince of Guangling should be established.
translations.idiomatic: If no other course is possible, the Prince of Guangling ought to be named heir.

sentences.zh: 若有異圖，禍難未已。

translations.literal: If there is a different scheme, calamity and disaster will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Any other choice would only prolong the crisis.

sentences.zh: 」絪等隨而唱之，眾議方定。

translations.literal: Yin and the others thereupon echoed him, and the assembly's deliberation was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin and the others promptly agreed, and consensus was reached.

sentences.zh: 及順宗在諒闇，外有王叔文輩操權樹黨，無復經制。

translations.literal: When Shunzong was in the mourning seclusion, outside there were Wang Shuwen and his kind seizing power and building factions, and no longer any adherence to classical norms.
translations.idiomatic: During Shunzong's mourning period, Wang Shuwen and his followers dominated court politics, forming factions and abandoning established governance.

sentences.zh: 次公與鄭絪同處內廷，多所匡正。

translations.literal: Cigong and Zheng Yin together dwelt within the inner court and corrected many matters.
translations.idiomatic: Serving together in the inner court, Cigong and Zheng Yin repeatedly set matters straight.

sentences.zh: 轉司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel's Meritorious Service Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Meritorious Service Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 久之，以本官知制誥，賜紫金魚袋，仍為學士，權知中書舍人。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was granted the additional duty of drafting imperial edicts in his present office, bestowed a purple-gold fish tally, and continued as academician, acting as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was entrusted with drafting edicts while retaining his rank, awarded the purple-gold fish tally, and continued at Hanlin while exercising the duties of Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 尋知禮部貢舉，斥浮華，進貞實，不為時力所搖。

translations.literal: Soon he oversaw the Ministry of Rites civil examinations, repudiating ornament and promoting integrity, not swayed by the power of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he supervised the civil service examinations for the Ministry of Rites, rejecting flashy candidates in favor of genuine talent and refusing to bow to prevailing pressures.

sentences.zh: 真拜中書舍人，仍充史館修撰，遷兵部侍郎、知制誥，復兼翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed Secretariat Drafter, still serving as compiler at the Historiography Institute, promoted to Vice Minister of War with edict-drafting duties, and again concurrently Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Formally confirmed as Secretariat Drafter, he continued compiling at the Historiography Institute, rose to Vice Minister of War while drafting edicts, and again held a concurrent Hanlin appointment.

sentences.zh: 與鄭絪善，會鄭絪罷相，次公左授太子賓客，改尚書右丞，兼判戶部事，拜陜、虢等州都防禦觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Zheng Yin; when Zheng Yin was dismissed as chief minister, Cigong was demoted by assignment to Household Companion of the Heir Apparent, changed to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, additionally administering Ministry of Public Revenue affairs, and appointed Commissioner for Overall Defense, Observation, and Disposition of Shaan, Guo, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: A close friend of Zheng Yin, he was reassigned when Yin left the chancellorship: first as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, then Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue with concurrent charge of public revenue, and finally as defense and observation commissioner over Shaan, Guo, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 請蠲錢三百萬，人得蘇息，政聞於朝。

translations.literal: He requested remission of three million in cash levies; the people were able to recover and breathe, and his governance was heard of at court.
translations.idiomatic: He secured cancellation of three million in cash taxes, giving the populace room to recover, and his record of governance reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 征為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 選人李勣、徐有功之孫，名在黜中，次公召而謂之曰：「子之祖先，勛在王府，豈限常格。

translations.literal: Among those being selected, Li Ji and Xu Yougong's grandson were listed among those to be dismissed; Cigong summoned them and said to them: "Your ancestors' merit lies in the princely household—how could they be bound by ordinary rules?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji and the grandson of Xu Yougong, though marked for elimination in the selection process, were called in by Cigong, who told them: "Your forebears served the imperial house with distinction—they should not be held to ordinary standards."

sentences.zh: 」並優秩而遣之。

translations.literal: Both were given preferential rank and sent on their way.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned them favorable appointments and released them.

sentences.zh: 改尚書左丞，恩顧頗厚。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; imperial favor toward him was quite generous.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, he enjoyed considerable imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 上方命為相，已命翰林學士王涯草詔。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to appoint him chief minister and had already ordered Hanlin Academician Wang Ya to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was on the verge of naming him chief minister and had already instructed Hanlin Academician Wang Ya to draft the appointment edict.

sentences.zh: 時淮夷宿兵歲久，次公累疏請罷。

translations.literal: At that time troops had been stationed against the Huai rebels for many years; Cigong repeatedly submitted memorials requesting their withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: With troops long garrisoned against the Huai rebels, Cigong sent memorial after memorial urging their recall.

sentences.zh: 會有捷書至，相詔方出，憲宗令追之。

translations.literal: It happened that a victory dispatch arrived; the chief-minister edict was just being issued when Xianzong ordered it recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Just as a victory report arrived and the appointment edict was about to be promulgated, Emperor Xianzong ordered it withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 遂出為淮南節度使、檢校工部尚書，兼揚州大都督府長史、御史大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as Military Governor of Huainan, Concurrent Minister of Works, concurrently Grand Prefect of Yangzhou Superior Prefecture and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he was dispatched as military governor of Huainan, with concurrent appointments as Minister of Works, grand prefect of Yangzhou, and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年十月，受代歸朝，道次病卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, upon being relieved and returning to court, he fell ill and died en route.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yuanhe 13, while traveling back to the capital after his term ended, he fell ill on the road and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，年六十六，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; he was sixty-six years old; his posthumous title was Jing ("Respectful").
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honored as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, he died at sixty-six and was given the posthumous name Jing, "The Respectful."

sentences.zh: 次公自少入仕，歷大寮，節操趨尚，始終如一，為眾推重。

translations.literal: From youth entering office through service in high ministries, Cigong's integrity and aims were always the same, and he was esteemed by all.
translations.idiomatic: From his first appointment through the highest offices, Cigong held to the same standards of conduct and was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 子洙，登進士第，尚憲宗女臨真公主。

translations.literal: His son Zhu passed the jinshi examination and married Emperor Xianzong's daughter, Princess Linzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu earned a jinshi degree and married Princess Linzhen, daughter of Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 累官至給事中、駙馬都尉、工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He accumulated offices up to Supervising Censor, Commander of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Guard, and Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to serve as supervising censor, commander of the imperial son-in-law's guard, and Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 鄭絪，字文明。

translations.literal: Zheng Yin, courtesy name Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin, whose courtesy name was Wenming.

sentences.zh: 父羨，池州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xian was Prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian served as prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 絪少有奇誌，好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Yin from youth had an extraordinary will, loved learning, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth Yin showed unusual ambition; he devoted himself to learning and wrote with considerable skill.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，有儒學高名如張參、蔣乂、楊綰、常袞，皆相知重。

translations.literal: During the Dali era, men of high repute in Confucian learning such as Zhang Can, Jiang Yi, Yang Wan, and Chang Gun all knew and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali period, leading Confucian scholars such as Zhang Can, Jiang Yi, Yang Wan, and Chang Gun all counted him a valued acquaintance.

sentences.zh: 絪擢進士第，登宏詞科，授秘書省校書郎、鄠縣尉。

translations.literal: Yin obtained the jinshi degree, passed the Macro-Phrases examination, and was appointed Collator in the Secretariat and Magistrate of Hu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yin passed the jinshi examinations and the Macro-Phrases test, then was appointed collator in the Secretariat and magistrate of Hu County.

sentences.zh: 張延賞鎮西川，辟為書記，入除補闕、起居郎，兼史職。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yanshang governed West Sichuan, he recruited him as secretary; upon entering the capital he was appointed Remonstrator and Diarist, concurrently holding a historiographical post.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited as secretary when Zhang Yanshang governed West Sichuan, he was later appointed remonstrator and diarist at court, with concurrent duties in the historiography office.

sentences.zh: 無幾，擢為翰林，轉司勛員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Hanlin, transferred to Vice Director of Meritorious Service, and granted edict-drafting duties.
translations.idiomatic: Within a short time he entered the Hanlin Academy, rose to vice director in the Meritorious Service Bureau, and took up edict drafting.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝，在內職十三年，小心兢謙，上遇之頗厚。

translations.literal: During Dezong's reign he held inner-court posts for thirteen years, cautious and reverently modest; the Emperor treated him quite generously.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Dezong's reign he served thirteen years in the inner court, meticulously careful and humble, and enjoyed substantial imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗初，勵精求理，絪與杜黃裳同當國柄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianzong's reign, when he strove to refine governance, Yin and Du Huangshang together held the reins of state.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianzong's reign, as the emperor worked to revitalize governance, Yin shared state power with Du Huangshang.

sentences.zh: 黃裳多所關決，首建議誅惠琳、斬劉辟及他制置。

translations.literal: Huangshang participated in deciding many matters; he first proposed executing Huilin, beheading Liu Pi, and other disposition measures.
translations.idiomatic: Huangshang took the lead on major decisions, including the executions of Huilin and Liu Pi and related military arrangements.

sentences.zh: 絪謙默多無所事，由是貶秩為太子賓客。

translations.literal: Yin was modest and reticent and for the most part had nothing to do; for this reason his rank was reduced and he was made Household Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, quietly unassertive and largely sidelined, was demoted to Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 出為嶺南節度觀察等使、廣州刺史、檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Military Governor and Observer of Lingnan and others, Prefect of Guangzhou, and Concurrent Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched as military governor and observer of Lingnan, prefect of Guangzhou, and concurrent Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以廉政稱。

translations.literal: He was known for incorrupt governance.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a reputation for clean administration.

sentences.zh: 為工部尚書，轉太常卿，又為同州刺史、長春宮使，改東都留守。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Works, transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then was Prefect of Tongzhou and Commissioner of the Changchun Palace, and changed to Protector of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as Minister of Works and then as Director of Imperial Sacrifices, he became prefect of Tongzhou and commissioner of the Changchun Palace before being appointed protector of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 入歷兵部尚書，旋為河中節度使。

translations.literal: Entering the capital, he served as Minister of War, and soon after was Military Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as Minister of War, he was soon sent out again as military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，入為御史大夫、檢校左僕射、兼太子少保。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, he entered the capital as Censor-in-Chief, Concurrent Left Grand Counselor, and Concurrent Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 he returned to court as Censor-in-Chief, with concurrent appointments as Left Grand Counselor and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 祗德子顥，登進士第，始綬弘文館校書。

translations.literal: Zhide's son Hao passed the jinshi examination and first received appointment as collator at the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, son of Zhide, earned his jinshi degree and was first appointed collator at the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 遷右拾遺、內供奉，詔授銀青光祿大夫，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Purifier and Inner Attendant; by edict he was granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and promoted to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to right purifier and inner attendant, he was by imperial edict made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and then promoted to diarist.

sentences.zh: 尚宣宗女萬壽公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Xuanzong's daughter, Princess Wanshou, and was appointed Commander of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Wanshou, daughter of Emperor Xuanzong, and was named commander of the imperial son-in-law's guard.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書郎、給事中、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of Secretariat Director, Supervising Censor, and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as a director in the secretariat, supervising censor, and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 典貢士二年，振拔滯才，至今稱之。

translations.literal: He presided over examination candidates for two years, lifting up neglected talent; to this day he is praised for it.
translations.idiomatic: During his two years overseeing the examinations he brought forward overlooked talent, a record still remembered with praise.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister in the Ministries of Justice and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大中十三年，檢校禮部尚書、河南尹。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dazhong, he was Concurrent Minister of Rites and Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 13 he held concurrent appointments as Minister of Rites and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 顥居戚裏，有器度。

translations.literal: Hao dwelt among the imperial affines and possessed breadth of character.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of the imperial family by marriage, Hao carried himself with measured dignity.

sentences.zh: 大中時，恩澤無對。

translations.literal: During the Dazhong era, his grace and favor had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong period no one in the realm matched the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 及宣宗棄代，追感恩遇，嘗為詩序曰：「去年壽昌節，赴麟德殿上壽，回憩於長興裏第。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong abandoned his generation, recalling the gratitude owed for his gracious treatment, he once wrote a preface to a poem, saying: "Last year on the Shouchang Festival, I went to offer birthday congratulations at the Linde Hall; on returning I rested at my residence in Changxing Lane."
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanzong's death, thinking back on the kindness he had received, he once wrote a preface to a poem: "Last year on the Shouchang Festival I went to the Linde Hall to offer birthday wishes; on my way back I stopped to rest at my house in Changxing Lane."

sentences.zh: 昏然晝寢，夢與十數人納涼於別館。

translations.literal: Drowsily he napped at midday and dreamed that he and a dozen or so people sought cool shade at a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He fell into a mid-day doze and dreamed of himself and a dozen companions escaping the heat at a detached pavilion.

sentences.zh: 館宇蕭灑，相與聯句。

translations.literal: The lodge building was spacious and elegant; together they linked lines of verse.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion was airy and serene, and they composed linked verses together.

sentences.zh: 予為數聯，同遊甚稱賞。

translations.literal: I contributed several couplets; my companions greatly praised and admired them.
translations.idiomatic: I supplied several lines, which my companions greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 既寤，不全記諸聯，唯省十字雲『石門霧露白，玉殿莓苔青』，乃書之於楹。

translations.literal: Upon waking I did not fully remember all the linked lines; I could recall only ten characters saying "At the stone gate, mist and dew are white; in the jade hall, moss and lichen are green," and so I wrote them on a pillar.
translations.idiomatic: When I awoke I could not remember the whole verse, but ten characters remained clear: "At the stone gate, mist and dew gleam white; in the jade hall, moss runs green." I wrote them on a column.

sentences.zh: 私怪語不祥，不敢言於人。

translations.literal: Privately I found the words inauspicious and did not dare speak of them to others.
translations.idiomatic: The lines struck me as ominous, and I kept them to myself.

sentences.zh: 不數日，宣宗不豫，廢朝會，及宮車上仙，方悟其事。

translations.literal: Within a few days Xuanzong was unwell, court audiences were suspended, and when the imperial carriage ascended to the immortals I only then understood the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Emperor Xuanzong fell ill and court sessions were suspended; when he died I finally understood what the dream had foretold.

sentences.zh: 追惟顧遇，續石門之句為十韻云：『間歲流虹節，歸軒出禁扃。

translations.literal: Recalling his gracious treatment, he continued the "stone gate" lines into ten rhymes, saying: "Years apart at the flowing-rainbow festival, returning carriage departing the forbidden gate-bolt."
translations.idiomatic: Remembering the emperor's kindness, he expanded the "stone gate" couplet into a ten-rhyme poem: "Another year at the rainbow-marked festival, my returning carriage passed beyond the palace gates."

sentences.zh: 奔波陶畏景，蕭灑夢殊庭。

translations.literal: Hurrying through the scorching sun of pottery-kiln heat, spacious and elegant in a dream of a separate courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: I rushed through blazing summer heat, yet in sleep wandered a pavilion of uncanny stillness.

sentences.zh: 境象非曾到，崇嚴昔未經。

translations.literal: Scenes and forms I had never before reached; lofty solemnity I had never previously traversed.
translations.idiomatic: None of it resembled any place I had known; the solemn grandeur was wholly unfamiliar.

sentences.zh: 日車烏斂翼，風動鶴飄翎。

translations.literal: The sun-chariot crow folded its wings; wind stirred and the crane's plumes fluttered.
translations.idiomatic: The sun-bird folded its wings; wind stirred the crane's drifting feathers.

sentences.zh: 異苑人爭集，涼臺筆不停。

translations.literal: In the separate garden people competed to gather; at the cool terrace the brush did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In that other garden companions crowded around; at the cool pavilion our brushes never rested.

sentences.zh: 石門霧露白，玉殿莓苔青。

translations.literal: At the stone gate, mist and dew are white; in the jade hall, moss and lichen are green.
translations.idiomatic: White mist clings to the stone gate; green moss covers the jade hall.

sentences.zh: 若匪災先兆，何當思入冥。

translations.literal: If it were not a prior sign of disaster, when would one think of entering the dark realm?
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been an omen of calamity, why would one dwell on the realm below?

sentences.zh: 禦鑢虛仗馬，華蓋負雲亭。

translations.literal: The imperial furnace empty, ceremonial horses in vain; the flowery canopy bears the cloud pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial hearth stood cold, the ceremonial horses unused; the canopy pavilion sank beneath cloud and shadow.

sentences.zh: 白日成千古，金滕閟九齡。

translations.literal: White day becomes a thousand ages; the golden casket is sealed for nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Daylight turned eternal night; the golden casket sealed away youth itself.

sentences.zh: 小臣哀絕筆，湖上泣青萍。

translations.literal: This minor official grieves with brush stilled; on the lake weeps over the green duckweed.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal subject lays down his brush in grief; by the lake he weeps for the drifting duckweed.

sentences.zh: 』」未幾，顥亦卒。

translations.literal: " Not long after, Hao also died.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Hao too passed away.

sentences.zh: 韋處厚，字德載，京兆人。

translations.literal: Wei Chuhou, courtesy name Dezai, was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chuhou, whose courtesy name was Dezai, came from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父萬，監察御史，為荊南節度參謀。

translations.literal: His father Wan was a Supervisory Censor and served as staff strategist for the Jingnan Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wan had been a supervisory censor and staff strategist to the military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 處厚本名淳，避憲宗諱，改名處厚。

translations.literal: Chuhou's original name was Chun; to avoid the taboo of Xianzong's name, he changed his name to Chuhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou had originally been named Chun but changed it to Chuhou to observe the taboo on Emperor Xianzong's personal name.

sentences.zh: 幼有至性，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: From childhood he had utmost nature; in serving his stepmother he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he showed exceptional character and was renowned for the filial devotion he showed his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 居父母憂，廬於墓次。

translations.literal: While dwelling in mourning for his parents, he built a hut at the graveside.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his parents he lived in a hut beside their tomb.

sentences.zh: 既免喪，遊長安。

translations.literal: Once the mourning period had ended, he traveled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he went to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 通《五經》，博覽史籍，而文思贍逸。

translations.literal: He mastered the Five Classics, broadly perused historical records, and his literary thought was ample and fluent.
translations.idiomatic: Fluent in the Five Classics and widely read in history, he wrote with rich and fluent ease.

sentences.zh: 元和初，登進士第，應賢良方正，擢居異等，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination, responded to the Worthy and Upright recruitment, was promoted to a superior grade, and was appointed Collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe era he earned his jinshi degree, distinguished himself in the Worthy and Upright examination, and was appointed collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 裴垍以宰相監修國史，奏以本官充直館，改咸陽縣尉，遷右拾遺，並兼史職。

translations.literal: Pei Ji, as chief minister supervising compilation of the National History, memorialized that he should fill his present office as a direct librarian, changed to Magistrate of Xianyang, promoted to Right Purifier, all concurrently holding historiographical posts.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Pei Ji, overseeing the national history, had him assigned as a direct librarian while retaining his rank; he was then made magistrate of Xianyang and promoted to right purifier, all while continuing historiographical work.

sentences.zh: 修《德宗實錄》五十卷上之，時稱信史。

translations.literal: He compiled fifty juan of the Veritable Records of Dezong and submitted them; at the time they were called trustworthy history.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled and submitted fifty fascicles of Emperor Dezong's Veritable Records, which contemporaries hailed as reliable history.

sentences.zh: 轉左補闕、禮部考功二員外。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Remonstrator and to both Vice Directorships in the Meritorious Achievement Bureau of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Remonstrator and to dual vice-director posts in the Ministry of Rites' Examination Bureau.

sentences.zh: 早為宰相韋貫之所重，時貫之以議兵不合旨出官，處厚坐友善，出為開州刺史。

translations.literal: Early on he was valued by Chief Minister Wei Guanzhi; at that time Guanzhi, because his military counsel did not accord with the imperial intent, was sent out of office, and Chuhou, implicated by friendship, was sent out as Prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guanzhi had long valued him; when Guanzhi was dismissed for military advice that displeased the throne, Chuhou was exiled to Kaizhou by association with his friend.

sentences.zh: 入拜戶部郎中，俄以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: Entering the capital, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Public Revenue; soon, in his present office, he was granted edict-drafting duties.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court as director in the Ministry of Public Revenue, he was soon entrusted with drafting imperial edicts as well.

sentences.zh: 穆宗以其學有師法，召入翰林，為侍講學士，換諫議大夫，改中書舍人，侍講如故。

translations.literal: Muzong, because his learning had teacherly method, summoned him into Hanlin as Lecturing Academician, exchanged him to Remonstrating Grandee, changed him to Secretariat Drafter, with lecturing as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong, impressed by the rigor of his scholarship, brought him into the Hanlin Academy as lecturing academician; he was made remonstrating grandee and then Secretariat Drafter while continuing to lecture at court.

sentences.zh: 時張平叔以便佞詼諧，他門捷進，自京兆少尹為鴻臚卿、判度支，不數月，宣授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Pingshu, by means of opportunism and witty levity, gained rapid advancement through other gates—from Metropolitan Vice Governor to Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations and Commissioner of the Revenue Bureau; within a few months he was directly appointed Vice Minister of Public Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pingshu, an adept flatterer with a gift for humor, rose by irregular paths—from vice governor of the capital to director of the court of diplomatic relations and revenue commissioner, and within months was directly appointed Vice Minister of Public Revenue.

sentences.zh: 平叔以征利中穆宗意，欲希大任。

translations.literal: Pingshu, by extracting profit in accord with Muzong's intent, wished to hope for a great appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Having won Muzong's favor through revenue schemes, Pingshu aspired to higher office.

sentences.zh: 以榷鹽舊法，為弊年深，欲官自糶鹽，可富國強兵，勸農積貨，疏利害十八條。

translations.literal: Considering that the old salt monopoly law had been a longstanding evil, he wished the state itself to sell salt, whereby the state could be enriched and the army strengthened, agriculture encouraged and goods accumulated; he submitted a memorial detailing eighteen points of benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Arguing that the old salt monopoly had long been corrupt, he proposed government direct sale of salt to enrich the state, strengthen the army, and promote agriculture; he submitted eighteen detailed points on the scheme's pros and cons.

sentences.zh: 詔下其奏，令公卿議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his memorial distributed and commanded the high ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor circulated his proposal and ordered the chief ministers to debate it.

sentences.zh: 處厚抗論不可，以平叔條奏不周，經慮未盡，以為利者返害，為簡者至煩，乃取其條目尤不可者，發十難以詰之。

translations.literal: Chuhou argued forcefully that it would not do; because Pingshu's itemized memorial was incomplete and its systematic considerations not exhaustive, what was taken for benefit would return as harm and what was taken for simplification would become vexation; he then took those items most impossible and issued ten difficulties to interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou forcefully opposed the plan, arguing that Pingshu's proposal was incomplete and ill-considered—that its promised benefits would become harms and its simplifications only create new burdens—and challenged ten of its most objectionable points in detail.

sentences.zh: 時平叔傾巧有恩，自謂言無不允。

translations.literal: At that time Pingshu was adept and favored, and considered that his words were never refused.
translations.idiomatic: Pingshu then enjoyed both imperial favor and a reputation for cleverness, and assumed his proposals would always prevail.

sentences.zh: 及處厚條件駁奏，穆宗稱善，令示平叔。

translations.literal: When Chuhou's itemized conditions refuting the memorial came, Muzong praised them and ordered them shown to Pingshu.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuhou's detailed rebuttal arrived, Muzong commended it and had it shown to Pingshu.

sentences.zh: 平叔詞屈無以答，其事遂寢。

translations.literal: Pingshu's words were beaten and he had nothing with which to reply; the matter thereupon was laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Pingshu was left speechless and could not answer; the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 處厚以幼主荒怠，不親政務，既居納誨之地，宜有以啟導性靈，乃銓擇經義雅言，以類相從，為二十卷，謂之《六經法言》，獻之。

translations.literal: Chuhou, because the young lord was dissolute and indolent and did not personally attend to state affairs, and since he occupied a place of receiving admonition, ought to have means to open and guide his spiritual nature; he therefore selected canonical meanings and refined words, arranged by category, making twenty scrolls called Six Classics Legal Words, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou saw that the young emperor was idle and neglectful of governance; as one whose duty was to counsel him, he compiled twenty scrolls of classical passages on moral conduct, organized by theme, titled "Legal Words of the Six Classics," and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 錫以繒帛銀器，仍賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was granted silk and silver vessels, and furthermore bestowed gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with silk and silver vessels and further conferred the gold-and-purple insignia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 以《憲宗實錄》未成，詔處厚與路隨兼充史館修撰。

translations.literal: Because the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong were not yet complete, an edict ordered Chuhou and Lu Sui additionally to serve as compilers in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong remained unfinished, Chuhou and Lu Sui were appointed adjunct compilers at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 實錄未成，許二人分日入內，仍放常參。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records not being complete, the two men were permitted to enter the palace on alternate days, and regular court attendance was waived for them.
translations.idiomatic: Until the work was done, they were allowed to enter the palace on alternate days and were excused from daily court attendance.

sentences.zh: 處厚俄又權兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Chuhou soon also served in an acting capacity as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Chuhou was also given acting appointment as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嗣位，李逢吉用事，素惡李紳，乃構成其罪，禍將不測。

translations.literal: When Jingzong succeeded to the throne, Li Fengji wielded power; he had long hated Li Shen and therefore fabricated his crime; calamity was about to be beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Li Fengji came to dominate court affairs; he had long detested Li Shen and now framed him for crimes, and Shen faced a fate that seemed beyond hope.

sentences.zh: 處厚與紳皆以孤進，同年進士，心頗傷之，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Chuhou and Shen had both advanced alone, jinshi of the same year; in their hearts they were quite pained at this, and thereupon submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou and Shen were both men who had risen without powerful patrons, and they had passed the jinshi examination in the same year; deeply troubled, Chuhou submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 臣竊聞朋黨議論，以李紳貶黜尚輕。

translations.literal: Your subject secretly hears that cliques in discussion consider Li Shen's demotion and dismissal still too light.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard whispers among factional circles that Li Shen's punishment was too lenient.

sentences.zh: 臣受恩至深，職備顧問，事關聖德，不合不言。

translations.literal: Your subject has received grace to the utmost depth; his office prepares him as adviser; the matter concerns the sage virtue; it is not fitting to remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has shown me extraordinary favor, and as your adviser I cannot keep silent when the imperial reputation is at stake.

sentences.zh: 紳先朝獎用，擢在翰林，無過可書，無罪可戮。

translations.literal: Shen in the former dynasty was rewarded and employed, promoted to Hanlin; there is no fault that can be recorded, no crime for which he can be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The previous emperor honored Li Shen and promoted him to the Hanlin Academy; he committed no recorded fault and deserved no punishment.

sentences.zh: 今群黨得誌，讒嫉大興。

translations.literal: Now the multitude of cliques have achieved their intent; slander and jealousy rise greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Now the factions have gotten their way, and slander and envy run rampant.

sentences.zh: 詢於人情，皆甚嘆駭。

translations.literal: Inquiring into human sentiment, all are greatly sighing and aghast.
translations.idiomatic: All who hear of it are shocked and dismayed.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「萋兮菲兮，成是貝錦。

translations.literal: The Odes says: "Luxuriant, unclean—thus is formed this brocade of shells."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "Woven from weeds, fashioned into precious brocade."

sentences.zh: 彼譖人者，亦已太甚。

translations.literal: Those who slander others—already too extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Those who weave such slander have gone too far.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「讒言罔極，交亂四國。

translations.literal: Again it says: "Slanderous words without limit, mutually disordering the four states."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Slander knows no bounds and throws kingdoms into chaos."

sentences.zh: 」自古帝王，未有遠君子近小人而致太平者。

translations.literal: From antiquity emperors and kings—never has one kept the noble at a distance and drawn the petty near and yet achieved great peace.
translations.idiomatic: No ruler in history has ever kept worthy men at arm's length while elevating petty schemers and still brought peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 古人云：「三年無改於父之道，可謂孝矣。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "Three years without altering the father's Way—this may be called filial."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "To govern for three years without deviating from one's father's principles—that is true filial piety."

sentences.zh: 」李紳是前朝任使，縱有罪愆，猶宜洗釁滌瑕，念舊忘過，以成無改之美。

translations.literal: Li Shen was an appointment and service of the former dynasty; even if there were faults and errors, still one ought to wash away offense and cleanse blemish, remember the old and forget wrongdoing, thereby to complete the beauty of non-alteration.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen served the previous reign faithfully; even if he had faults, Your Majesty should cleanse his name, remember past service, and forgive past errors—fulfilling the ideal of filial governance.

sentences.zh: 今逢吉門下故吏，遍滿朝行，侵毀加誣，何詞不有？

translations.literal: Now Fengji's former subordinates from his household fill the court ranks; they add calumny to injury and slander—what words are there that they do not have?
translations.idiomatic: Fengji's former underlings now fill the ranks of government; they pile calumny upon slander with accusations of every kind.

sentences.zh: 所貶如此，猶為太輕。

translations.literal: The demotion being such as this, still it is too light.
translations.idiomatic: Given such treatment, his punishment is still considered too lenient.

sentences.zh: 蓋曾參有投杼之疑，先師有拾塵之戒。

translations.literal: For Zeng Shen had the suspicion of casting away the shuttle; the former teacher had the warning of picking up dust.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zeng Shen once fell under false suspicion, and Confucius himself warned against repeating hearsay.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下斷自聖慮，不惑奸邪，則天下幸甚！

translations.literal: Prostrate, I hope Your Majesty will decide from sage deliberation, not be confused by treacherous evil—then all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will judge this matter with your own wisdom and not be misled by deceitful men. The realm would be most fortunate.

sentences.zh: 建中之初，山東向化，只緣宰相朋黨，上負朝廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, Shandong turned toward transformation—solely because of cliques among chief ministers who above betrayed the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianzhong era, when Shandong's provinces had begun to submit, chief ministerial factions betrayed the throne and brought ruin upon the realm.

sentences.zh: 楊炎為元載復讎，盧杞為劉晏報怨，兵連禍結，天下不平。

translations.literal: Yang Yan avenged Yuan Zai, Lu Qi repaid a grudge for Liu Yan; warfare linked and calamity bound—the realm was not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan took revenge for Yuan Zai, Lu Qi struck back for Liu Yan—war followed war until the empire was left in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 伏乞聖明，察臣愚懇。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I beg the sage clarity to examine your subject's foolish earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty's wise attention to my humble plea.

sentences.zh: 帝悟其事，紳得減死，貶端州司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor comprehended the matter; Shen obtained reduction from death and was demoted to Staff Officer of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood the situation; Li Shen was spared execution and demoted to staff officer at Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 處厚正拜兵部侍郎，謝恩於思政殿。

translations.literal: Chuhou received formal appointment as Vice Minister of War and gave thanks for grace at Sizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou was formally appointed Vice Minister of War and gave thanks at Sizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 時昭湣狂恣，屢出畋遊。

translations.literal: At that time Zhaomin was wild and unrestrained, repeatedly going out to hunt and roam.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhaomin Emperor was wild and unrestrained, going on hunting excursions again and again.

sentences.zh: 每月坐朝不三四日。

translations.literal: Each month he sat at court audience no more than three or four days.
translations.idiomatic: He held court only three or four days a month.

sentences.zh: 處厚因謝，從容奏曰：「臣有大罪，伏乞面首。

translations.literal: Chuhou, on the occasion of giving thanks, calmly submitted saying: "Your subject has a great crime; prostrate, I beg to speak face to head."
translations.idiomatic: During the audience, Chuhou spoke calmly: "Your Majesty, I have committed a grave offense and beg leave to confess it openly."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何也？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What is it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "What offense?"

sentences.zh: 」處厚對曰：「臣前為諫官，不能先朝死諫，縱先聖好畋及色，以至不壽，臣合當誅。

translations.literal: Chuhou replied saying: "Your subject formerly served as remonstrator; he could not at the prior court remonstrate unto death; he indulged the former sage's love of hunting and of color, leading to short life; your subject ought properly to be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou replied: "When I served as a remonstrating official under your predecessor, I failed to speak out even at the cost of my life. I allowed the late emperor's love of hunting and pleasure to shorten his days—I deserve death for that."

sentences.zh: 然所以不死諫者，亦為陛下此時在春宮，年已十五。

translations.literal: Yet the reason he did not remonstrate unto death was also because Your Majesty at that time was in the Eastern Palace, age already fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I held back because Your Majesty was then in the Eastern Palace, already fifteen years old.

sentences.zh: 今則陛下皇子始一歲矣，臣安得更避死亡之誅？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's imperial son is only one year old; how can your subject further avoid the punishment of death?
translations.idiomatic: But now Your Majesty's heir is only one year old. How can I shy away from speaking the truth even if it costs me my life?

sentences.zh: 」上深感悟其意，賜錦彩一百匹、銀器四事。

translations.literal: The sovereign deeply comprehended and was moved by his meaning; he bestowed one hundred bolts of brocade and four items of silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, the emperor rewarded him with a hundred bolts of brocade and four silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年四月，群臣上尊號，禦殿受冊肆赦。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Baoli, the multitude of ministers presented a honorific title; at the imperial hall he received the patent and broadly granted amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Baoli 1, the court presented a honorific title to the emperor, who accepted it in formal ceremony and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉以李紳之故，所撰赦文但雲左降官已經量移者與量移，不言未量移者，蓋欲紳不受恩例。

translations.literal: Li Fengji, because of Li Shen, in the amnesty text he drafted only said that demoted officials who had already been transferred by degree would receive degree transfer, not speaking of those not yet transferred—presumably wishing Shen not to receive the grace precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Li Shen, Li Fengji drafted the amnesty text so that only officials who had already been moved nearer to the capital could be transferred again—not those who had never received such relief—apparently to keep Shen from benefiting.

sentences.zh: 處厚上疏曰：「伏見赦文節目中，左降官有不該恩澤者。

translations.literal: Chuhou submitted a memorial saying: "Prostrate, I see that in the sections of the amnesty text, demoted officials have some who do not fall within grace and favor."
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou submitted a memorial: "I notice that some demoted officials are excluded from the amnesty's benefits."

sentences.zh: 在宥之體，有所未弘。

translations.literal: The substance of being lenient in confinement had something not yet enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of imperial clemency is not fully embodied here.

sentences.zh: 臣聞物議皆言逢吉恐李紳量移，故有此節。

translations.literal: Your subject hears that public discussion all says Fengji feared Li Shen's degree transfer, therefore there is this section.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion holds that Fengji added this clause specifically to block Li Shen's transfer.

sentences.zh: 若如此，則應是近年流貶官，因李紳一人皆不得量移。

translations.literal: If it is such as this, then it should be that in recent years exiled and demoted officials, because of Li Shen alone, all cannot receive degree transfer.
translations.idiomatic: If so, then every recently exiled official would be denied transfer because of one man—Li Shen.

sentences.zh: 事體至大，豈敢不言？

translations.literal: The substance of the matter is to the utmost great; how dare one not speak?
translations.idiomatic: This is a matter of great consequence. How could I remain silent?

sentences.zh: 李紳先朝獎任，曾在內廷，自經貶官，未蒙恩宥。

translations.literal: Li Shen in the former dynasty was rewarded and entrusted, once in the inner court; since his demotion he has not received grace and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen was honored and trusted in the previous reign and served in the inner court; since his demotion he has received no pardon.

sentences.zh: 古人云：『人君當記人之功，忘人之過。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "A lord of men ought to remember men's achievements and forget men's faults."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "A ruler should remember service and forget offenses."

sentences.zh: 』管仲拘囚，齊桓舉為國相；

translations.literal: Guan Zhong was bound in imprisonment; Duke Huan of Qi raised him as state chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong was once a prisoner, yet Duke Huan of Qi made him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 冶長縲紲，仲尼選為密親。

translations.literal: Ye Chang was in fetters and chains; Zhongni selected him as close intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Chang was bound in chains, yet Confucius chose him as a close companion.

sentences.zh: 有罪猶宜滌蕩，無辜豈可終累？

translations.literal: If there is guilt still one ought to wash clean; if innocent how can one be finally encumbered?
translations.idiomatic: Even the guilty deserve a fresh start; surely the innocent should not suffer perpetual punishment?

sentences.zh: 況鴻名大號，冊禮重儀，天地百靈之所鑒臨，億兆八纮之所瞻戴。

translations.literal: Moreover the great name and great title, the weighty rites of investiture—what the hundred spirits of Heaven and Earth observe and regard, what the hundred millions of the eight directions look up to and bear upon their heads.
translations.idiomatic: This is an occasion of great honorific titles and solemn investiture rites, witnessed by Heaven and Earth and watched by all the realm.

sentences.zh: 恩澤不廣，實非所宜。

translations.literal: Grace and favor not broad—truly not what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: A narrow amnesty is hardly fitting for such an occasion.

sentences.zh: 臣與逢吉素無讎嫌，與李紳本非親黨，所論者全大體，所陳者在至公，伏乞聖慈察臣肝膽。

translations.literal: Your subject with Fengji from of old has no feud or suspicion; with Li Shen originally is not kin or clique; what is discussed embraces the great principle; what is set forth lies in utmost public-mindedness; prostrate, I beg the sage compassion to examine your subject's liver and gall.
translations.idiomatic: I bear Fengji no personal grudge and share no faction with Li Shen. I speak only for the good of the realm, and I beg Your Majesty to see the sincerity of my counsel.

sentences.zh: 倘蒙允許，仍望宣付宰臣，應近年左降官，並編入赦條，令準舊例，得量移近處。

translations.literal: If perchance granted permission, still hope to proclaim and deliver to chief ministers: all demoted officials of recent years, together entered into amnesty articles, ordered according to old precedent to obtain degree transfer to near places.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty agrees, I ask that recent demotions be included in the amnesty and that officials be allowed, according to precedent, to be transferred nearer to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」帝覽奏其事，乃追改赦文，紳方沾恩例。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed the memorial on the matter; thereupon revised the amnesty text; Shen then touched the grace precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and revised the amnesty text, and Li Shen finally received the benefit.

sentences.zh: 處厚為翰林承旨學士，每立視草，愜會聖旨。

translations.literal: Chuhou served as Hanlin Chief Academician; each time he stood viewing the draft, it accorded with and met the sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: As chief Hanlin academician, Chuhou drafted imperial edicts that consistently matched the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 常奉急命於宣州征鷹鷙及楊、益、兩浙索奇文綾錦，皆抗疏不奉命，且引前時赦書為證，帝皆可其奏。

translations.literal: He often received urgent orders from Xuanzhou to levy fierce hawks and eagles, and from Yang, Yi, and the two Zhes to demand strange-patterned silk brocades; all he forcefully memorialized refusing to obey commands, moreover citing the former amnesty edict as proof; the emperor all approved his memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to requisition hunting hawks from Xuanzhou or rare brocades from Yangzhou, Yizhou, and the two Zhe provinces, he repeatedly submitted memorials refusing, citing the emperor's own past amnesty edicts; the emperor accepted each time.

sentences.zh: 寶歷季年，急變中起。

translations.literal: In the final year of Baoli, sudden change arose amid crisis.
translations.idiomatic: In the last year of the Baoli era, crisis struck suddenly.

sentences.zh: 文宗底綏內難，詔命將降，未有所定。

translations.literal: Wenzong attained the throne amid internal difficulty; edict commands were about to descend, but nothing was yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Wenzong took the throne amid internal turmoil, edicts needed to be drafted but none had yet been settled.

sentences.zh: 處厚聞難奔赴，昌言曰：「《春秋》之法，大義滅親，內惡必書，以明逆順。

translations.literal: Chuhou, hearing of the difficulty, rushed to the scene and spoke forthrightly saying: "The method of the Spring and Autumn Annals: great righteousness extinguishes kin; inner evil must be recorded, thereby to clarify rebellion and compliance."
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou rushed to the palace and declared boldly: "The Spring and Autumn Annals teaches that righteousness outweighs kinship and that internal treachery must be recorded to distinguish loyal from rebel."

sentences.zh: 正名討罪，於義何嫌？

translations.literal: Correct naming and punishing crime—in righteousness what suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: To name the crime and punish the guilty—where is the offense in that?

sentences.zh: 安可依違，有所避諱！

translations.literal: How can one comply and resist, having avoidance and taboo!
translations.idiomatic: How can we hesitate or euphemize?

sentences.zh: 」遂奉籓教行焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he received and carried out the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial edict was drafted and issued accordingly.

sentences.zh: 是夕，詔命制置及踐祚禮儀，不暇責所司，皆出於處厚之議。

translations.literal: That evening, edict commands for arrangements and accession rites—there was no leisure to assign blame to the offices; all issued from Chuhou's deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: That same night, every arrangement for the succession and coronation rites, with no time to consult the usual offices, came from Chuhou's recommendations.

sentences.zh: 及禮行之後，皆葉舊章。

translations.literal: When the rites had been performed, all were abandoned from old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremonies were complete, the makeshift procedures were set aside.

sentences.zh: 以佐命功，旋拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事、監修國史，加銀青光祿大夫，進爵靈昌郡公。

translations.literal: For assisting-destiny merit, he was soon appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrently Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Supervisor of the Compilation of National History; added Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; advanced in noble rank to Duke of Lingchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in the succession he was promptly made Vice Director of the Secretariat, chief minister, and supervisor of the national history, with the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and promoted to Duke of Lingchang.

sentences.zh: 處厚在相位，務在濟時，不為身計。

translations.literal: Chuhou in the chancellor's position, his task lay in aiding the age; he did not calculate for himself.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Chuhou devoted himself to the needs of the times rather than his own advancement.

sentences.zh: 中外補授，鹹得其宜。

translations.literal: Interior and exterior appointments and grants—all obtained their fitness.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments throughout the government were made appropriately.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元中，宰相齊抗奏減冗員，罷諸州別駕，其在京百司，當入別駕者，多處之朝列。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Zhenyuan era, Chief Minister Qi Kang memorialized to reduce redundant posts and abolish the vice prefects of various prefectures; those in the hundred offices at the capital who ought to enter vice prefect posts were mostly placed in the court columns.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhenyuan era, Chief Minister Qi Kang had reduced redundant posts by abolishing vice-prefect positions across the provinces; officials in the capital who would have filled those posts were instead kept in court ranks.

sentences.zh: 元和以來，兩河用兵，偏裨立功者，往往擢在周行。

translations.literal: From the Yuanhe era onward, with warfare in the two He regions, lower officers who achieved merit were often promoted into the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yuanhe era, military officers from the Hebei region who distinguished themselves in the two-river campaigns were often promoted into central court posts.

sentences.zh: 率以儲采王官雜補之，皆盛服趨朝，硃紫填擁。

translations.literal: Generally they were filled by reserve talents, royal officials, and miscellaneous supplements; all in full dress hastened to court; vermilion and purple filled and pressed together.
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies were filled with assorted reserve officials and junior appointees, all of whom appeared at court in formal regalia until crimson and purple robes crowded the halls.

sentences.zh: 久次當進，及受代閑居者，常數十人，趨中書及宰相私第，摩肩候謁，繁於辭語。

translations.literal: Those long in rank who ought to advance, and those who had received replacement and dwelt idle—often several tens of men—hurried to the Secretariat and chief ministers' private residences, shoulder to shoulder waiting to pay respects, elaborate in pleading speech.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of men awaiting promotion or between assignments crowded the Secretariat and chief ministers' private residences, jostling for audiences and pleading endlessly for appointments.

sentences.zh: 及處厚秉政，復奏置六雄、十望、十緊、三十四州別駕以處之。

translations.literal: When Chuhou held governance, he again memorialized to establish vice prefects for the six great, ten prominent, ten critical, and thirty-four prefectures to place them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chuhou took power, he restored vice-prefect posts in the six "great," ten "prominent," ten "critical," and thirty-four other key prefectures to absorb these officials.

sentences.zh: 而清流不雜，朝政清肅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the pure stream was not mixed; court governance was pure and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: The result was a cleaner court hierarchy and more orderly governance.

sentences.zh: 文宗勤於聽政，然浮於決斷，宰相奏事得請，往往中變。

translations.literal: Wenzong was diligent in hearing governance, yet floated in decision; when chief ministers submitted affairs and obtained permission, often midway it changed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was attentive in court but impulsive in judgment; he often reversed decisions after initially approving the chief ministers' recommendations.

sentences.zh: 處厚常獨論奏曰：「陛下不以臣等不肖，用為宰相，參議大政。

translations.literal: Chuhou often alone submitted discussion saying: "Your Majesty, not considering your subjects unworthy, employed us as chief ministers to participate in deliberating great governance."
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou once submitted a memorial alone: "Your Majesty appointed us as chief ministers despite our inadequacies to help govern the realm."

sentences.zh: 凡有奏請，初蒙聽納，尋易聖懷。

translations.literal: Whenever there were submitted requests, at first granted listening acceptance; soon the sage mind changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet time and again Your Majesty initially approves our recommendations only to change your mind shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 若出自宸衷，即示臣等不信；

translations.literal: If it issued from the imperial breast, this shows your subjects are not trusted.
translations.idiomatic: If these reversals come from Your Majesty's own judgment, it suggests you do not trust us.

sentences.zh: 若出於橫議，臣等何名鼎司？

translations.literal: If it issued from unauthorized discussion, what name do your subjects have as tripod ministers?
translations.idiomatic: If they come from outside interference, what purpose do we serve as chief ministers?

sentences.zh: 且裴度元勛宿德，歷輔四朝，孜孜竭誠，人望所屬，陛下固宜親重。

translations.literal: Moreover Pei Du is original merit and longstanding virtue, having assisted four reigns; tirelessly he exhausts sincerity; the people's hopes belong to him; Your Majesty ought indeed to draw close and value him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du is a veteran statesman who has served four emperors with tireless devotion and enjoys the people's trust—Your Majesty should rely on him.

sentences.zh: 竇易直良厚，忠事先朝，陛下固當委信。

translations.literal: Dou Yizhi is good and generous; he loyally served the prior court; Your Majesty ought indeed to entrust and trust him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yizhi is virtuous and loyal, having served the previous reign faithfully—Your Majesty should trust him as well.

sentences.zh: 微臣才薄，首蒙陛下擢用，非出他門，言既不從，臣宜先退。

translations.literal: This humble subject's talent is thin; first receiving Your Majesty's elevation and employment, not emerging from other gates; words already not followed—I ought first to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: As for myself, I lack talent yet was elevated by Your Majesty's own choice. If my counsel is disregarded, I should be the first to resign.

sentences.zh: 」即趨下再拜陳乞。

translations.literal: Immediately he hastened down and twice bowed stating his request.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped down and prostrated himself, asking to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 上矍然曰：「何至此耶！

translations.literal: The sovereign started and said: "How did it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Startled, the emperor exclaimed: "How can you speak of resigning!"

sentences.zh: 卿之誌業，朕素自知，登庸作輔，百職斯舉。

translations.literal: Your intent and achievement—We from of old know it ourselves; mounting and employing you as aide—all hundred offices thereby are raised.
translations.idiomatic: I have always known your character and ability; I elevated you to help govern, and under you the administration has flourished.

sentences.zh: 縱朕有所失，安可遽辭，以彰吾薄德？

translations.literal: Even if We have some failing, how can you abruptly resign, thereby to display Our thin virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Even if I sometimes err, how can you resign and thereby expose my faults to the world?

sentences.zh: 」處厚謝之而去，出延英門，復令召還。

translations.literal: Chuhou thanked him and departed; going out the Yanying Gate, again he was ordered summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou withdrew, but after he had passed through the Yanying Gate the emperor had him recalled.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「凡卿所欲言，並宜啟論。

translations.literal: He said to him: "Whatever you wish to speak—all ought to be opened in discussion."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "Speak freely on whatever is on your mind."

sentences.zh: 」處厚因對彰善癉惡，歸之法制，凡數百言。

translations.literal: Chuhou thereupon in reply made manifest good and concealed evil, returning it to law and system—all several hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou proceeded to deliver a lengthy discourse on rewarding virtue and punishing vice according to law—several hundred words in all.

sentences.zh: 又裴度勛高望重，為人盡心切直，宜久任，可壯國威。

translations.literal: Again: Pei Du's merit is high and hopes heavy; as a man he exhausts heart with utmost directness; he ought to serve long; he can strengthen the state's prestige.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Pei Du's distinguished service and forthright character warranted a long tenure to bolster the nation's authority.

sentences.zh: 帝皆聽納。

translations.literal: The emperor all listened and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 自是宰臣敷奏，人不敢橫議。

translations.literal: From this time chief ministers presenting memorials—people did not dare unauthorized discussion.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no one dared interfere when the chief ministers presented their business to the throne.

sentences.zh: 俄而滄州李同捷叛，朝廷加兵。

translations.literal: Soon Cangzhou's Li Tongjie rebelled; the court increased troops.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Tongjie of Cangzhou rebelled, and the court mobilized forces against him.

sentences.zh: 魏博史憲誠，中懷向背，裴度以宿舊自任，待憲誠於不疑。

translations.literal: Weibo's Shi XianCheng—in his inner heart faced both ways; Pei Du, taking himself for an old acquaintance, treated XianCheng without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Shi XianCheng of Weibo was equivocal in his loyalties, yet Pei Du, trusting their longstanding relationship, treated him without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣親吏請事至中書。

translations.literal: Once he sent a close clerk to request business at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: XianCheng once sent a personal clerk to the Secretariat on official business.

sentences.zh: 處厚謂曰：「晉公以百口於上前保爾使主，處厚則不然，但仰俟所為，自有朝典耳。

translations.literal: Chuhou said to him: "The Duke of Jin with a hundred mouths before the sovereign guaranteed you as military commissioner; Chuhou is not such—only look up and await what is done; naturally there are court statutes."
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou told the clerk: "Lord Pei staked his reputation before the throne to vouch for your master—but I make no such guarantee. I will judge your master's conduct by the court's laws alone."

sentences.zh: 」憲誠聞之大懼，自此輸竭，竟有功於滄州。

translations.literal: XianCheng, hearing this, was greatly afraid; from this time he contributed exhaustively; in the end he had merit at Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When XianCheng heard this he was terrified and thereafter gave his full support, eventually contributing to the victory at Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又嘗以理財制用為國之本，撰《太和國計》二十卷以獻。

translations.literal: Again he once, taking regulation of wealth and control of expenditure as the root of the state, compiled twenty scrolls of Tahe National Accounts and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled twenty scrolls on state finance titled "National Accounts of the Tahe Era," arguing that fiscal management was the foundation of governance, and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 李載義累破滄、鎮兩軍，兵士每有俘執，多遣刳剔。

translations.literal: Li Zaiyi repeatedly broke the Cang and Zhen two armies; whenever soldiers had captives taken, many were sent to gouge and flay.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi, in repeated victories over the Cangzhou and Zhenzhou armies, allowed his troops to mutilate prisoners—gouging and flaying them.

sentences.zh: 處厚以書喻之，載義深然其旨。

translations.literal: Chuhou by letter instructed him; Zaiyi deeply accorded with its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou wrote to reprove him, and Li Zaiyi deeply accepted his point.

sentences.zh: 自此滄、鎮所獲生口，配隸遠地，前後全活數百千人。

translations.literal: From this time Cang and Zhen captives taken alive were assigned and registered in distant places; before and after, fully living numbered several hundred to a thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter prisoners from the Cangzhou and Zhenzhou campaigns were assigned to distant regions instead of being killed, saving hundreds of lives.

sentences.zh: 處厚居家循易，如不克任。

translations.literal: Chuhou at home followed ease; as if unable to bear responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: At home Chuhou lived simply and unassumingly, as though unaware of his own importance.

sentences.zh: 至於廷諍敷啟，及馭轄待胥吏，勁確嶷然不可奪。

translations.literal: As for remonstrating at court and presenting guidance, and managing jurisdiction in dealing with clerks—he was firm, exact, and towering, such that nothing could be wrested away.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at court, in remonstrance and counsel, and in managing his subordinates and clerks, he was so firm and incorruptible that no one could sway him.

sentences.zh: 質狀非魁偉，如甚懦者；

translations.literal: His physical form was not tall and imposing; he seemed very much a timid man.
translations.idiomatic: He was neither tall nor imposing in bearing; he appeared almost timid.

sentences.zh: 而庶僚請事，畏惕相顧，雖與語移晷，不敢私謁。

translations.literal: Yet when junior officials requested audience, they feared and watched one another; even if talking until the sundial moved a gnomon-shadow, they did not dare private audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when subordinates came to his office on business, they were so awed that even after lengthy interviews they would not dare visit him privately.

sentences.zh: 急於用才，酷嗜文學。

translations.literal: He was urgent in employing talent; he passionately loved literature.
translations.idiomatic: He was eager to promote talent and deeply devoted to literary culture.

sentences.zh: 嘗病前古有以浮議坐廢者，故推擇群材，往往棄瑕錄用，亦為時所譏。

translations.literal: Once he grieved that in former ages there were those who, because of empty talk, sat and were dismissed; therefore in selecting and choosing groups of talents, he often discarded flaws and recorded them for employment—this too was ridiculed by the times.
translations.idiomatic: Disturbed that worthy men of the past had been ruined by idle gossip, he often overlooked minor faults when recommending people for office—a practice some contemporaries criticized.

sentences.zh: 雅信釋氏因果，晚年尤甚。

translations.literal: He elegantly believed in the Buddhist teaching of cause and effect; in his later years this was especially so.
translations.idiomatic: He was a sincere believer in Buddhist karma, a faith that grew stronger in his later years.

sentences.zh: 聚書逾萬卷，多手自刊校。

translations.literal: He amassed books exceeding ten thousand scrolls; many he personally collated and proofread.
translations.idiomatic: He collected more than ten thousand scrolls of books, many of which he personally edited and proofread.

sentences.zh: 奉詔修《元和實錄》，未絕筆，其統例取舍，皆處厚創起焉。

translations.literal: By imperial order he revised the Veritable Records of the Yuanhe Era; before the brush was laid down, the system and principles of selection and rejection—all Chuhou initiated.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compile the Veritable Records of the Yuanhe Era, he had established its editorial standards and principles before his death.

sentences.zh: 太和二年十二月，因延英奏對，造膝之際，忽奏「臣病作」，遽退。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Tahe, during a Yan Ying Hall memorial response, at the moment of close approach to the knee, suddenly he memorialized "Your subject's illness has begun," and hastily withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of the Tahe reign, during an audience in the Yan Ying Hall, he suddenly exclaimed that he had taken ill and hastily withdrew just as he reached the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 文宗命中官扶出，歸第一夕而卒，年五十六，贈司空。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong ordered palace attendants to support him out; returning to his residence, the first night he died, age fifty-six; posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong sent eunuchs to assist him out of the hall. He died that very night at home, aged fifty-six. He was posthumously awarded the title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 處厚當國柄二周歲，啟沃之謀，頗協時譽，鹹共惜之。

translations.literal: Chuhou held state power for two full years; his nourishing counsel largely accorded with the times' reputation; all together regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou had held the reins of government for two years, and his counsel had won wide acclaim. All mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 崔群，字敦詩，清河武城人，山東著姓。

translations.literal: Cui Qun, courtesy name Dunshi, a man of Wucheng in Qinghe—a distinguished surname of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun, courtesy name Dunshi, was from Wucheng in Qinghe, a prominent Shandong clan.

sentences.zh: 十九登進士第，又制策登科，授秘書省校書郎，累遷右補闕。

translations.literal: At nineteen he ascended the jinshi degree; again in the decree examination he passed; granted Collator in the Secretariat; repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he passed the jinshi examination and then the special decree examination. He was appointed Collator in the Secretariat and eventually rose to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 元和初，召為翰林學士，歷中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, summoned as Hanlin Academician; served as Drafting Officer of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanhe era he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy and later served as Drafting Officer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 群在內職，常以讜言正論聞於時。

translations.literal: Qun in inner service, often by forthright words and upright discourse was heard in the times.
translations.idiomatic: In his palace posts, Cui Qun earned renown for candid and principled counsel.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘉賞，降宣旨云：「自今後學士進狀，並取崔群連署，然後進來。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong commended and rewarded, issued edict instruction saying: "From now on when academicians submit memorials, all must take Cui Qun's joint signature, then submit them."
translations.idiomatic: Pleased with his service, Emperor Xianzong decreed: "Henceforth all memorials from Hanlin academicians must bear Cui Qun's countersignature before submission."

sentences.zh: 」群以禁密之司，動為故事，自爾學士或惡直醜正，則其下學士無由上言。

translations.literal: Qun, because this was a forbidden and secret office, once established would become precedent; from then academicians who hated directness and resented rectitude—their subordinate academicians had no means to speak above.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun argued that the Hanlin Academy was a confidential institution and that such a rule would become permanent precedent, allowing senior academicians who resented honest advisers to block memorials from their juniors.

sentences.zh: 群堅不奉詔，三疏論奏方允。

translations.literal: Qun firmly would not obey the edict; three memorials arguing and presenting before it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused to comply and only after three memorials of protest did the emperor relent.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Second year seventh month, appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Yuanhe, he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，誅李師道，上顧謂宰臣曰：「李師古雖自襲祖父，然朝廷待之始終。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, Li Shidao was executed; the emperor turned and said to chief ministers: "Although Li Shigu by himself inherited grandfather, yet the court treated him from beginning to end."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, after Li Shidao was put to death, the emperor turned to his chief ministers and said: "Though Li Shigu seized his post from his grandfather, the court treated his family honorably throughout."

sentences.zh: 其妻於師道即嫂叔也，雖雲逆族，若量罪輕重，亦宜降等。

translations.literal: His wife toward Shidao was sister-in-law and uncle; although called a rebel clan, if measuring crime's weight and lightness, also ought to be reduced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: "His wife was Li Shidao's sister-in-law—a relationship that, though tainted by rebellion, warrants a lesser penalty when the crimes are weighed."

sentences.zh: 又李宗奭雖抵嚴憲，其情比之大逆，亦有不同。

translations.literal: Again Li Zongyi, although striking against strict statutes, his situation compared to great treason also has difference.
translations.idiomatic: "Li Zongyi violated the law, but his offense was not comparable to treason in the fullest sense."

sentences.zh: 其妻士族也，今其子女俱在掖廷，於法皆似稍深。

translations.literal: His wife was a gentry clan; now her sons and daughters all were in the palace women's quarters; by law all seemed somewhat deep.
translations.idiomatic: "His wife was of good family, yet her children are now held in the palace prisons—the legal penalties seem somewhat harsh."

sentences.zh: 卿等留意否？

translations.literal: Have you, sirs, taken note or not?
translations.idiomatic: "Have you given this attention?"

sentences.zh: 」群對曰：「聖情仁惻，罪止元兇。

translations.literal: Qun replied saying: "Sacred sentiment is humane and compassionate; crime stops at the chief culprit."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun replied: "Your Majesty's mercy is well placed—the guilt should fall only on the ringleaders."

sentences.zh: 其妻近屬，倘獲寬宥，實合弘煦之道。

translations.literal: Their wives as close kin—if permitted leniency, truly fits the way of great warmth.
translations.idiomatic: "If their wives and close kin receive clemency, that would accord with your benevolent rule."

sentences.zh: 」於是師古妻裴氏、女宜娘，詔出於鄧州安置。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shigu's wife Lady Pei and daughter Yiniang—edict issued to release to Dengzhou for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict ordered Li Shigu's wife Lady Pei and daughter Yiniang released and resettled in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 宗奭妻韋氏及男女，先沒掖廷，並釋放；

translations.literal: Zongyi's wife Lady Wei and sons and daughters, first seized into palace quarters, all released.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongyi's wife Lady Wei and their children, who had been imprisoned in the palace quarters, were also freed.

sentences.zh: 其奴婢、資貨皆復賜之。

translations.literal: Their slave-servants and property—all again bestowed to them.
translations.idiomatic: Their servants and possessions were restored to them as well.

sentences.zh: 又鹽鐵福建院官權長孺坐贓，詔付京兆府決殺。

translations.literal: Again Salt and Iron Fujian Office official Quan Changru sat in embezzlement; edict delivered to the Capital Prefecture for sentence and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Also, Quan Changru, an official of the Fujian Salt and Iron Commission, was convicted of corruption and ordered to be executed by the Capital Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長孺母劉氏求哀於宰相，群因入對言之。

translations.literal: Changru's mother Lady Liu begged for pity from the chief ministers; Qun, on entering for audience, spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Changru's mother Lady Liu pleaded with the chief ministers, and Cui Qun raised the matter during an imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 憲宗湣其母耄年，乃曰：「朕將屈法赦長孺何如？

translations.literal: Xianzong pitied his mother's aged years, then said: "I shall bend the law and pardon Changru—how about that?"
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the aged mother's plea, Emperor Xianzong said: "What if I bend the law and pardon Changru?"

sentences.zh: 」群曰：「陛下仁惻即赦之，當速令中使宣諭。

translations.literal: Qun said: "Your Majesty, if compassionate and pardoning him, ought quickly to order a palace envoy to proclaim the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun replied: "If Your Majesty intends mercy, you should dispatch a palace envoy at once to announce the pardon."

sentences.zh: 如待正敕，即無及也。

translations.literal: If waiting for the formal edict, then there will be no time.
translations.idiomatic: "If you wait for the formal decree, it will be too late."

sentences.zh: 」長孺竟得免死長流。

translations.literal: Changru in the end obtained exemption from death, long exile.
translations.idiomatic: Changru was spared execution and sentenced instead to long exile.

sentences.zh: 群之啟奏平恕，多此類也。

translations.literal: Qun's memorials opening and presenting were mild and forgiving—many were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Cui Qun's memorials displayed this same spirit of lenient justice.

sentences.zh: 時憲宗急於蕩寇，頗獎聚斂之臣。

translations.literal: At that time Xianzong was urgent to sweep away bandits; he rather rewarded those who amassed and collected.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xianzong was eager to suppress rebellions and tended to reward officials skilled at revenue extraction.

sentences.zh: 故籓府由是希旨，往往捃拾，目為進奉。

translations.literal: Therefore regional headquarters from this followed intent; often they gathered and picked up, termed as tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier governors accordingly curried favor, gathering funds and calling them "tribute" to the throne.

sentences.zh: 處州刺史苗稷進羨余錢七千貫，群議以為違詔，受之則失信於天下，請卻賜本州，代貧下租稅。
