translations.literal: Chuzhou Prefect Miao Ji presented surplus money of seven thousand strings; Qun's council considered this violated the edict; accepting it would lose trust before all under Heaven; requested return and grant to the prefecture, substituting for the poor and low classes' rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuzhou Prefect Miao Ji submitted seven thousand strings of surplus revenue, Cui Qun argued that accepting it would violate imperial policy and damage the throne's credibility. He recommended returning the funds to subsidize local taxes for the poor.

sentences.zh: 時論美之。

translations.literal: Contemporary discourse praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion praised his decision.

sentences.zh: 度支使皇甫镈陰結權幸，以求宰相，群累疏其奸邪。

translations.literal: Fiscal Commissioner Huangfu Bo secretly joined with favored powers, to seek the chief ministership; Qun repeatedly memorialized his treachery and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Fiscal Commissioner Huangfu Bo curried favor with powerful courtiers in hopes of becoming chief minister, and Cui Qun repeatedly memorialized against his corruption.

sentences.zh: 嘗因對面論，語及天寶、開元中事，群曰：「安危在出令，存亡系所任。

translations.literal: Once, because of face-to-face discussion, speech reached Taibao and Kaiyuan-era affairs; Qun said: "Security and danger lie in issuing orders; survival and extinction depend on those appointed."
translations.idiomatic: During one audience on affairs of the Tianbao and Kaiyuan eras, Cui Qun said: "A dynasty's fate rests on its policies and on the men entrusted with power."

sentences.zh: 玄宗用姚崇、宋璟、張九齡、韓休、李元纮、杜暹則理；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong employed Yao Chong, Song Jing, Zhang Jiuling, Han Xiu, Li Yuanhong, Du Xian—then there was order.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong used men like Yao Chong, Song Jing, Zhang Jiuling, Han Xiu, Li Yuanhong, and Du Xian, the realm was well governed.

sentences.zh: 用林甫、楊國忠則亂。

translations.literal: Employed Lin Fu, Yang Guozhong—then there was disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When he employed Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong, it fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 人皆以天寶十五年祿山自范陽起兵，是理亂分時，臣以為開元二十年罷賢相張九齡，專任奸臣李林甫，理亂自此已分矣。

translations.literal: People all take the fifteenth year of Tianbao when Lu Shan from Fanyang raised troops as the time order and disorder divided; your subject considers the twentieth year of Kaiyuan, dismissing worthy chief minister Zhang Jiuling, exclusively employing treacherous minister Li Linfu—order and disorder from this were already divided.
translations.idiomatic: Most believe the turning point came in Tianbao 15, when An Lushan rebelled from Fanyang. But I hold that the decline began in Kaiyuan 20, when the worthy Zhang Jiuling was dismissed and the corrupt Li Linfu was given sole power.

sentences.zh: 用人得失，所系非小。

translations.literal: Employing men—gain and loss—the connection is not small.
translations.idiomatic: The choice of ministers is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 」詞意激切，左右為之感動。

translations.literal: His words' meaning was fierce and urgent; those at his sides were moved by it.
translations.idiomatic: His words were so passionate that those present were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 镈深恨之。

translations.literal: Bo deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo came to hate him deeply.

sentences.zh: 而憲宗終用镈為宰相。

translations.literal: Yet Xianzong in the end employed Bo as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Xianzong ultimately appointed Huangfu Bo as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 無何，群臣議上尊號，皇甫镈欲加「孝德」兩字，群曰：「有睿聖，則孝德在其中矣。

translations.literal: Before long, the assembled ministers discussed ascending honorific title; Huangfu Bo wished to add the two characters "Filial Virtue"; Qun said: "Having Sagacious Sagehood, then Filial Virtue is already within it."
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when the court debated an honorific title for the emperor, Huangfu Bo proposed adding the characters for "Filial Virtue." Cui Qun objected: "With 'Sagacious Sagehood' already included, filial virtue is implied."

sentences.zh: 」竟為镈所構。

translations.literal: In the end he was framed by Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was ruined by Huangfu Bo's intrigues.

sentences.zh: 憲宗不樂，出為湖南觀察都團練使。

translations.literal: Xianzong was displeased; he was sent out as Hunan Observation and Grand Training Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong, displeased, sent him out to serve as Military Governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，征拜吏部侍郎，召見別殿，謂群曰：「我升儲位，知卿為羽翼。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; summoned to audience in a separate hall, said to Qun: "When I rose to the heirship, I knew you as my wing."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong came to the throne, Cui Qun was recalled as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel. Received in a private audience, the emperor said: "When I was named heir, I knew you had been my supporter."

sentences.zh: 」群曰：「先帝之意，元在陛下。

translations.literal: Qun said: "The late emperor's intent originally was on Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun replied: "The late emperor's intention had always been to install Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 頃者授陛下淮西節度使，臣奉命草制，且曰：『能辨南陽之牘，允符東海之貴。

translations.literal: Recently, when Your Majesty was granted Huai Xi Military Commissioner, your subject received order to draft the decree, and it said: 'Able to distinguish Nanyang's documents, truly matching the Donghai's nobility.'
translations.idiomatic: When you were appointed military governor of Huai West, I drafted the edict, which praised your ability to 'discern the petitions of Nanyang and fulfill the dignity of the Eastern Sea'—

sentences.zh: 』若不知先帝深旨，臣豈敢輕言？

translations.literal: If not knowing the late emperor's deep intent, would your subject dare speak lightly?
translations.idiomatic: Had I not understood the late emperor's deeper meaning, I would never have written such words.

sentences.zh: 」數日，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Within days, appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 浹旬，授檢校兵部尚書，兼徐州刺史、武寧軍節度、徐泗濠觀察等使。

translations.literal: Within ten days, granted honorary Minister of War, concurrently Xuzhou Prefect, Wuning Army Military Commissioner, and Xu-Si-Hao Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was made honorary Minister of War and Military Governor of Wuning, with concurrent jurisdiction over Xuzhou and the Xu-Si-Hao region.

sentences.zh: 初，幽、鎮逆命，詔授沂州刺史王智興為武寧軍節度副使，領徐州兵討伐。

translations.literal: Initially, You and Zhen defied orders; edict granted Yizhou Prefect Wang Zhixing as Wuning Army Vice Military Commissioner, leading Xuzhou troops to suppress and attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhou and Zhenzhou rebelled, Wang Zhixing of Yizhou was appointed vice military commissioner of Wuning and ordered to lead Xuzhou troops against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 群以智興早得士心，表請因授智興旄鉞，竟寢不報。

translations.literal: Qun, because Zhixing early gained soldiers' hearts, memorialized requesting therefore to grant Zhixing command banner and axe; in the end the petition slept without response.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun, noting that Zhixing already enjoyed the troops' loyalty, recommended appointing him full military commissioner—but the request was never answered.

sentences.zh: 智興自河北回戈，城內皆是父兄，開關延入，群為智興所逐。

translations.literal: Zhixing from Hebei turned his blades back; within the city all were fathers and elder brothers; opened the gate and extended welcome in; Qun was by Zhixing driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing then turned his army from Hebei back upon Xuzhou—the garrison, many his kinsmen, opened the gates to him, and Cui Qun was driven out.

sentences.zh: 朝廷坐其失守，授秘書監，分司東都。

translations.literal: The court held him responsible for losing defense; granted Director of the Palace Library, assigned to the Eastern Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: The court held him responsible for the loss of the city and appointed him Director of the Palace Library in an honorary post at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改華州刺史、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long, changed to Huazhou Prefect, concurrently Censor Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Prefect of Huazhou and Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 復改宣州刺史、歙池等州都團練觀察等使，徵拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Again changed to Xuanzhou Prefect and Grand Training and Observation Commissioner of She and Chi prefectures; summoned and appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Xuanzhou as military governor of the She-Chi region, then recalled as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 久之，改檢校吏部尚書、江陵尹、荊南節度觀察使。

translations.literal: After long time, changed to honorary Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Jiangling Prefect, and Jingnan Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became honorary Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Prefect of Jiangling, and Military Governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，改檢校右僕射，兼太常卿。

translations.literal: Passing a year, changed to honorary Right Vice Director and concurrently Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，拜檢校左僕射，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Fifth year of Tahe, appointed honorary Left Vice Director, concurrently Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Tahe reign he was appointed honorary Left Vice Director and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 六年八月卒，年六十一，冊贈司空。

translations.literal: Sixth year eighth month died, age sixty-one; enfeoffed posthumously as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the sixth year, aged sixty-one, and was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 群有沖識精裁，為時賢相。

translations.literal: Qun had serene insight and refined judgment; he was a worthy chief minister of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun possessed discerning judgment and was regarded as a worthy chief minister of his age.

sentences.zh: 清議以儉素之節，其終不及厥初。

translations.literal: Pure critics, regarding his frugal and plain integrity, considered his end did not reach his beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Purists noted that he had begun with a reputation for austerity but did not uphold it to the end.

sentences.zh: 群年未冠舉進士，陸贄知舉，訪於梁肅，議其登第有才行者，肅曰：「崔群雖少年，他日必至公輔。

translations.literal: Qun, before the capping age, entered the jinshi examination; Lu Zhi supervised the examination, inquired of Liang Su concerning those who passed with talent and conduct; Su said: "Although Cui Qun is young, another day he will surely reach chief minister and assistant."
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Qun took the jinshi examination before coming of age, Chief Examiner Lu Zhi asked Liang Su which candidates showed both talent and character. Su replied: "Though Cui Qun is still young, he will one day reach the highest offices."

sentences.zh: 」果如其言。

translations.literal: Indeed it matched his words.
translations.idiomatic: And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 群弟於，登進士，官至郎署，有令名。

translations.literal: Qun's younger brother Yu passed the jinshi; office reached the secretariat bureaus; he had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Cui Yu also passed the jinshi examination, rose to a post in the secretariat, and enjoyed a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 子充，亦以文學進，歷三署，終東都留守。

translations.literal: His son Chong also by literary learning advanced; served in the three bureaus; ended as Eastern Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cui Chong also rose through literary achievement, served in the three central bureaus, and eventually became Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 路隨，字南式，其先陽平人。

translations.literal: Lu Sui, courtesy name Nanshi, his ancestors were men of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui, courtesy name Nanshi, was descended from Yangping.

sentences.zh: 高祖節，高宗朝為越王府東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jie, in Emperor Gaozong's reign served as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Yue's household.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Lu Jie served in Emperor Gaozong's reign as Libationer in the household of the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 曾祖惟恕，官至睦州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Weishu, office reached Mu Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Lu Weishu rose to Prefect of Mu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖俊之，仕終太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Junzhi, in office ended as Palace Receptionist for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lu Junzhi served ultimately as Palace Receptionist to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 父泌，字安期，少好學，通《五經》，尤嗜《詩》、《易》、《左氏春秋》，能諷其章句，皆究深旨。

translations.literal: His father Bi, courtesy name Anqi, from youth loved learning; mastered the Five Classics; especially fond of the Odes, Changes, and Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals; able to recite their passages and clauses—all investigated deep meaning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lu Bi, courtesy name Anqi, was a devoted scholar versed in the Five Classics, with particular mastery of the Book of Odes, the Book of Changes, and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, which he knew in full depth.

sentences.zh: 博涉史傳，工五言詩。

translations.literal: Broadly traversed historical biographies; skilled in five-character verse.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read in history and a skilled writer of regulated verse.

sentences.zh: 性端亮寡言，以孝悌聞於宗族。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and bright, few in words; by filial piety and brotherly respect he was known in the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and reticent, he was renowned within his clan for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 建中末，以長安尉從調，舉李益、韋綬等書判同居高第，泌授城門郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianzhong, as Chang'an Assistant he followed transfer; in the examination with Li Yi, Wei Shou, and others for document judgment, he shared top rank; Bi was granted Gate Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianzhong era, while serving as an assistant in Chang'an, he ranked at the top of the document-judgment examination alongside Li Yi and Wei Shou and was appointed Gate Commandant.

sentences.zh: 屬德宗違難奉天，泌時在京師，棄妻子潛詣行在所。

translations.literal: It happened that Dezong met calamity at Fengtian; Bi was then in the capital; he abandoned wife and children and secretly went to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian, Bi was in the capital. He left his family behind and secretly made his way to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 又從幸梁州，排潰軍而出，再為流矢所中，裂裳濡血。

translations.literal: Again he followed the emperor's visit to Liangzhou; pushing through routed troops to get out, twice struck by stray arrows; tore his robe soaked with blood.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Liangzhou, forcing his way through fleeing troops and twice being struck by stray arrows, his torn robes soaked in blood.

sentences.zh: 以策說渾瑊，瑊深重之，辟為從事。

translations.literal: By stratagem he persuaded Hun Zhen; Zhen deeply valued him and recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Impressing General Hun Zhen with his counsel, he was taken on as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 瑊討懷光，累奏為副元帥判官、檢校戶部郎中、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Zhen attacked Huai Guang; repeatedly memorialized him as Deputy Commander's administrative officer, honorary Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During Hun Zhen's campaign against Zhu Huaiguang, Bi was repeatedly recommended and appointed deputy commander staff officer, honorary Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 河中平，隨瑊與吐蕃會盟於平涼，因劫盟陷蕃。

translations.literal: When Hexi was pacified, following Zhen he joined the Tibetans in alliance at Pingliang; because of the abducted alliance, he fell into Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Hezhong, he accompanied Hun Zhen to a peace conference with Tibet at Pingliang and was seized when the Tibetans broke the truce.

sentences.zh: 在絕域累年，棲心於釋氏之教，為贊普所重，待以賓禮，卒於戎鹿。

translations.literal: In the far frontier for accumulated years, he settled his heart in the Buddhist teaching; by the tsenpo he was valued, treated with guest rites; he died at Ronglu.
translations.idiomatic: Held captive in Tibet for many years, he devoted himself to Buddhism, earned the Tibetan king's respect, was treated as an honored guest, and died at Ronglu.

sentences.zh: 貞元十九年，吐蕃遺邊將書求和。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year of Zhenyuan, Tibet sent the border general a letter seeking peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Zhenyuan reign, Tibet sent a letter to a border general proposing peace.

sentences.zh: 隨哀泣上疏，願允其請。

translations.literal: Sui, weeping in grief, submitted a memorial, wishing to grant their request.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui, weeping, submitted a memorial asking that the request be granted.

sentences.zh: 表三上，德宗命中使諭旨。

translations.literal: Memorials thrice submitted; Dezong ordered a palace envoy to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: After three memorials, Emperor Dezong sent a palace envoy to convey his response.

sentences.zh: 朝廷懲其宿詐，俟更要於後信，訖數歲不報。

translations.literal: The court, chastened by their long-standing deception, awaited further requirements for later trust; until several years, no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Distrustful of Tibet's past treachery, the court withheld approval for several years.

sentences.zh: 元和中，蕃使復款塞，隨復五獻封章，請修和好。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Tibetan envoys again paid respects at the frontier passes; Sui again five times submitted sealed memorials, requesting restoration of friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era, when Tibetan envoys again appeared at the frontier, Lu Sui submitted five sealed memorials urging reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 又上書於宰執哀訴。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a letter to the chief executors, grieving and pleading.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote directly to the chief ministers in an anguished appeal.

sentences.zh: 裴垍、李籓皆協力敷奏，憲宗可之。

translations.literal: Pei Ji and Li Fan both together exerted force in presenting memorials; Xianzong approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji and Li Fan joined in pressing the case, and Emperor Xianzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 命祠部郎中徐復報聘，乃特於詔中疏平涼陷蕃者名氏，令歸中國。

translations.literal: Ordered Director of Sacrificial Affairs Xu Fu to return the diplomatic visit; then especially in the edict listed the names of those who fell into Tibet at Pingliang, ordering their return to China.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu of the Ministry of Rites was sent as envoy, and the edict specifically named those captured at Pingliang and ordered their repatriation.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃因復等還，遣使來朝。

translations.literal: Tibet, because Fu and others returned, dispatched envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet then sent an embassy to court in response.

sentences.zh: 遂以泌及鄭叔矩之喪與銘及遺錄至，朝野傷嘆。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bi's and Zheng Shuju's remains, with epitaphs and posthumous records, arrived; court and countryside mourned and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: The remains of Lu Bi and Zheng Shuju, together with their epitaphs and writings, were returned, moving the entire court to grief.

sentences.zh: 憲宗憫之，贈絳州刺史，賜絹二百匹。

translations.literal: Xianzong pitied him; granted Jiangzhou Prefect posthumously; bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Moved with pity, Emperor Xianzong posthumously appointed Lu Bi Prefect of Jiangzhou and granted two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 至葬日，委所在官給喪事。

translations.literal: When the burial day arrived, entrusted to the local officials to supply funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial, local officials were ordered to provide for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 泌累贈太子少保。

translations.literal: Bi, on successive posthumous occasions, was granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bi was posthumously promoted on several occasions to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 泌陷蕃之歲，隨方在孩提；

translations.literal: In the year Bi fell into Tibet, Sui was still in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Bi was captured by Tibet, Lu Sui was still an infant.

sentences.zh: 後稍長成，知父在蕃，乃日夜啼號，坐必西向，饌不食肉，母氏言其形貌肖先君，遂終身不照鏡。

translations.literal: Later, as he gradually grew up, knowing his father was in Tibet, he day and night wept and wailed; whenever he sat he faced west; at meals he ate no meat. His mother said his features resembled his late father, and so all his life he never looked in a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older and learned that his father was captive in Tibet, he wept constantly, always sat facing west, and refused meat at meals. His mother said he resembled his late father so closely that he never looked in a mirror for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 後以通經調授潤州參軍，為李锜所困。

translations.literal: Later, through mastery of the classics he was transferred and appointed Runzhou Assistant Military Officer; he was harassed by Li Ge.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the classics examination he was posted as an aide in Runzhou, where Li Ge made life difficult for him.

sentences.zh: 使知市事，隨翛然坐市中，一不介意。

translations.literal: [Li Ge] had him oversee market affairs; Sui calmly sat in the marketplace, not caring in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ge put him in charge of the market, but Lu Sui simply sat there at ease, wholly unperturbed.

sentences.zh: 韋夏卿為東都留守，聞而辟之，由是聲名日振。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaqing was Eastern Capital garrison commander; hearing of him, he recruited him; from this his reputation daily flourished.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Xiaqing became Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital, he recruited Lu Sui on hearing of him, and his reputation steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 元和五年，邊吏以訃至。

translations.literal: Fifth year of Yuanhe, border officials brought the death notice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yuanhe reign, a border official brought word of Lu Bi's death.

sentences.zh: 隨居喪，益以孝聞。

translations.literal: Sui observed mourning; all the more for filial piety he was known.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui observed mourning for his father and became still more renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 服闋，擢拜左補闕。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was promoted and appointed Left Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 會李絳諷上納諫，憲宗皇帝曰：「諫官路隨、韋處厚章疏相繼，朕常深用其言。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Jue indirectly urged the emperor to accept remonstrance; Emperor Xianzong said: "Remonstrance officials Lu Sui and Wei Chuhou have submitted memorials one after another; I often deeply use their words."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jue urged the emperor to heed remonstrance, Emperor Xianzong said: "The censors Lu Sui and Wei Chuhou have submitted one memorial after another, and I have often taken their counsel deeply to heart."

sentences.zh: 」自是識者敬伏焉。

translations.literal: From this, those who understood bowed in respect.
translations.idiomatic: From that time those in the know held them in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 俄遷起居郎，轉司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long promoted to Diarist; transferred to outside director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Diarist and then transferred to an outside director's post in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 自補闕至司勛員外，皆充史館修撰。

translations.literal: From Remonstrance Official to outside director in the Ministry of Personnel—all served as History Office compiler.
translations.idiomatic: From his appointment as remonstrance official through his post in the Ministry of Personnel, he concurrently served as a compiler at the History Office.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，遷司勛郎中，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel; granted vermilion fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong came to the throne, Lu Sui was made a director in the Ministry of Personnel and granted the vermilion fish tally of third rank.

sentences.zh: 與韋處厚同入翰林為侍講學士。

translations.literal: Together with Wei Chuhou entered the Hanlin Academy as Lecturing Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy together with Wei Chuhou as a lecturing academician.

sentences.zh: 采三代皇王興衰，著《六經法言》二十卷奏之。

translations.literal: Gathering the rise and fall of emperors and kings through the Three Dynasties, he composed "Legal Words of the Six Classics" in twenty scrolls and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the rise and fall of royal houses from the Three Dynasties onward, he wrote twenty scrolls of "Legal Maxims of the Six Classics" and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 拜諫議大夫，依前侍講學士。

translations.literal: Appointed Remonstrance Grandee; as before Lecturing Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Remonstrance Grandee while continuing as lecturing academician.

sentences.zh: 將修《憲宗實錄》，復命兼充史職。

translations.literal: When about to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong, again ordered concurrently to fill the history post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong were to be compiled, he was again ordered to hold a concurrent post as historian.

sentences.zh: 敬宗登極，拜中書舍人、翰林學士，仍賜紫。

translations.literal: When Jingzong ascended the throne, appointed Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician; still granted purple.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong came to the throne, Lu Sui was made Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician and granted the purple robe.

sentences.zh: 有以金帛謝除制者，必叱而卻之曰：「吾以公事接私財耶？

translations.literal: When anyone brought gold and silk to thank him for drafting their appointment decree, he always rebuked and refused them, saying: "Do I conduct official business while accepting private wealth?"
translations.idiomatic: When anyone offered gold or silk to thank him for drafting an appointment decree, he always rejected them sharply: "Am I to handle official business while taking private gifts?"

sentences.zh: 」終無所納。

translations.literal: In the end he accepted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He never accepted a single gift.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，韋處厚入相，隨代為承旨，轉兵部侍郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Wei Chuhou entered the chancellery; Sui replaced him as Chief Academician, transferred to Vice Minister of War, Director of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, Wei Chuhou entered the chancellery and Lu Sui succeeded him as chief academician, becoming Vice Minister of War and Director of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，處厚薨，隨代為相，拜中書侍郎，加監修國史。

translations.literal: Second year of Tahe, Chuhou died; Sui replaced him as chief minister, appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, additionally Supervisor of National History compilation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tahe reign, after Wei Chuhou's death Lu Sui succeeded him as chief minister, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and made Supervisor of the National History.

sentences.zh: 初，韓愈撰《順宗實錄》，說禁中事頗切直內官惡之，往往於上前言其不實，累朝有詔改修。

translations.literal: Initially, Han Yu compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Shunzong; in speaking of inner-palace affairs he was quite blunt and direct. Inner eunuchs hated this and often before the emperor said it was untrue; through successive reigns there were edicts ordering revision.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Yu had compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Shunzong, writing bluntly about inner-palace affairs. The eunuchs resented this and repeatedly told successive emperors the account was false, and several reigns issued edicts ordering revisions.

sentences.zh: 及隨進《憲宗實錄》後，文宗復令改正永貞時事，隨奏曰：

translations.literal: After Sui submitted the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong, Wenzong again ordered correction of affairs from the Yongzhen era; Sui memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Sui submitted the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong, Emperor Wenzong again ordered revisions to events of the Yongzhen era. Lu Sui memorialized in reply:

sentences.zh: 臣昨面奉聖旨，以《順宗實錄》頗非詳實，委臣等重加刊正，畢日聞奏。

translations.literal: Your subject yesterday personally received the sacred edict that the Veritable Records of Emperor Shunzong are quite not detailed and true, entrusting your subjects to heavily revise and correct, reporting when complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I received Your Majesty's edict stating that the Veritable Records of Emperor Shunzong are insufficiently accurate and directing us to undertake a thorough revision, with a report due upon completion.

sentences.zh: 臣自奉宣命，取史本欲加筆削。

translations.literal: Your subject, from receiving the promulgated order, took the history manuscript intending to add cuts and emendations.
translations.idiomatic: Since receiving that order I have taken up the manuscript with the intention of revising it.

sentences.zh: 近見衛尉卿周居巢、諫議大夫王彥威、給事中李固言、史官蘇景胤等各上章疏，具陳刊改非甚便宜。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen Commandant of Guards Zhou Juchao, Remonstrance Grandee Wang Yanwei, Recipient of Petitions Li Guyin, and historian Su Jingyin each submit memorials, fully stating that revision is not very expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Zhou Juchao, Minister of the Guard; Wang Yanwei, Remonstrance Grandee; Li Guyin, Recipient of Petitions; and the historian Su Jingyin have each submitted memorials arguing that revision would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 又聞班行如此議論頗眾。

translations.literal: Again I hear among the court ranks such discussion is quite numerous.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard much similar talk among officials at court.

sentences.zh: 臣伏以史冊之作，勸誡所存，事有當書，理宜歸實。

translations.literal: Your subject submits that the writing of historical annals exists for admonition and warning; where events ought to be recorded, reason requires returning to truth.
translations.idiomatic: Historical writing exists to instruct and admonish: what ought to be recorded must be grounded in fact.

sentences.zh: 匹夫美惡尚不可誣，人君得失無容虛載。

translations.literal: Even the good and evil of common men cannot be slandered; the gains and losses of rulers cannot tolerate false recording.
translations.idiomatic: The virtues and faults of ordinary men must not be falsely reported—how much less may a ruler's achievements and failures be invented?

sentences.zh: 聖旨以前件《實錄》記貞元末數事，稍非摭實，蓋出傳聞，審知差舛，便令刊正。

translations.literal: The sacred edict, regarding the former Veritable Records' recording of several affairs at the end of the Zhenyuan era, said they were somewhat not gathered from fact, probably arising from hearsay; knowing the errors, ordered revision.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's edict noted that certain entries on late Zhenyuan events in the earlier Veritable Records appear not to be solidly grounded in fact but drawn from rumor, and once these errors were verified, ordered their correction.

sentences.zh: 頃因坐日，屢形聖言，通計前後，至於數四。

translations.literal: Recently because of sitting days, your sacred words repeatedly appeared; counting front and back, reaching to four or five times.
translations.idiomatic: In recent audiences Your Majesty has raised this matter repeatedly—four or five times in all.

sentences.zh: 臣及宗閔、僧孺亦以永貞已來，歲月至近，禁中行事，在外固難詳知。

translations.literal: Your subject, together with Zongmin and Sengru, also take the view that since Yongzhen, the years and months are recent; inner-palace conduct—those outside naturally find it hard to know in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin, Niu Sengru, and I have likewise noted that since the Yongzhen era the events in question are recent, and palace affairs are naturally difficult for outsiders to know in detail.

sentences.zh: 陛下所言，皆是接於耳目。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty spoke—all were matters reaching your ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty recounted came from your own direct experience.

sentences.zh: 既聞乖謬，因述古今，引前史直不疑盜嫂之言，及第五倫撾公之說，皆多此比類，難盡信書。

translations.literal: Having heard errors, you then recounted past and present, citing former histories—the tale of Zhi Buyi and the stolen sister-in-law, and Diwu Lun beating the duke—all largely such analogies, hard to fully trust the written record.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of these discrepancies, Your Majesty drew on history, citing such cases as the charge that Zhi Buyi stole his sister-in-law and the story of Diwu Lun beating the duke—examples of the sort of hearsay that often finds its way into historical texts and cannot always be trusted.

sentences.zh: 所冀睿鑒詳於聽言，深宮慎於行事。

translations.literal: What is hoped is that sagacious discernment scrutinizes what is heard, and the deep palace is cautious in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: I only hope that Your Majesty's discerning judgment will weigh such testimony carefully and that palace conduct will remain circumspect.

sentences.zh: 持此比類，上開聰明，特蒙降察，稍恕前謬。

translations.literal: Holding to such analogies, you opened your clarity above; we specially received lowered scrutiny, slightly pardoning earlier errors.
translations.idiomatic: By these examples Your Majesty showed your clear understanding, and in your gracious reconsideration you have somewhat excused the earlier errors.

sentences.zh: 由是近垂宣命，令有改修。

translations.literal: From this, recently an edict was issued, ordering revision.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the recent order to proceed with revision.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏以貞觀已來，累朝實錄有經重撰，不敢固辭。

translations.literal: Your subjects submit that since the Zhenguan era, successive reigns' Veritable Records have sometimes been rewritten; we dare not firmly refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenguan era, Veritable Records of several reigns have been rewritten; we would not presume to refuse outright.

sentences.zh: 但欲粗刪深誤，亦固盡存諸說。

translations.literal: But we wish only roughly to delete deep errors, and still firmly preserve all accounts.
translations.idiomatic: We propose only to remove the most serious errors while preserving alternative accounts wherever possible.

sentences.zh: 宗閔、僧孺相與商量，緣此書成於韓愈，今史官李漢、蔣系皆愈之子婿，若遣參撰，或致私嫌。

translations.literal: Zongmin and Sengru consulted together: because this book was completed by Han Yu, the current historians Li Han and Jiang Xi are both Han Yu's sons-in-law; if sent to join compilation, private bias might arise.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin, Niu Sengru, and I discussed the matter: since the original work was Han Yu's, and the historians Li Han and Jiang Xi are both Han Yu's sons-in-law, their participation might invite suspicion of partiality.

sentences.zh: 以臣既職監修，盍令詳正，及經奏請，事遂施行。

translations.literal: Since your subject already holds the post of supervising compiler, why not have [me] thoroughly correct it; after memorial and request, the matter was then implemented.
translations.idiomatic: As I already supervise the compilation, I proposed to undertake the corrections myself; once the memorial was submitted, the plan was put into effect.

sentences.zh: 今者庶僚競言，不知本起，表章交奏，似有他疑。

translations.literal: Now junior officials compete in speaking, not knowing how it began; memorials cross and submit, as if there were other suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Now many officials are speaking out without knowing how the project began, and their overlapping memorials suggest other motives are at work.

sentences.zh: 臣雖至昧，容非自請。

translations.literal: Your subject, though utterly obscure, perhaps did not request this of my own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am hardly a man of keen insight, I assure Your Majesty this was not my own idea.

sentences.zh: 既迫群議，輒冒上聞。

translations.literal: Pressed by the multitude of opinion, I rashly presume to report above.
translations.idiomatic: Compelled by widespread concern, I venture to report this to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 縱臣果獲修成，必懼終為時累。

translations.literal: Even if your subject should indeed complete the revision, I would surely fear becoming a burden to the times in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I should succeed in completing the revision, I fear I would ultimately become a liability to the court.

sentences.zh: 且韓愈所書，亦非己出，元和之後，已是相循。

translations.literal: Moreover, what Han Yu wrote was not entirely his own composition; after the Yuanhe era, it was already passed down in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Han Yu's text was not wholly his own original work—after the Yuanhe era it had already been transmitted through several hands.

sentences.zh: 縱其密親，豈害公理？

translations.literal: Even if his close kinsmen [work on it], how would that harm public principle?
translations.idiomatic: Even if his close relations serve as historians, what harm does that do to impartial truth?

sentences.zh: 使歸本職，實謂正名。

translations.literal: Having them return to their original posts—this truly may be called correcting names.
translations.idiomatic: Returning them to their ordinary duties would in truth be to set matters right.

sentences.zh: 其《實錄》伏望條示舊記最錯誤者，宣付史官，委之修定。

translations.literal: As for the Veritable Records, your subjects humbly hope Your Majesty will list the most erroneous passages of the old record, promulgate them to the historians, and entrust revision to them.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully ask that Your Majesty identify the most erroneous passages in the old record, assign them to the historians, and entrust the revision to them.

sentences.zh: 則冀聖祖垂休，永無慚於傳信。

translations.literal: Then we hope the sage ancestor will extend his blessings, forever without shame in transmitting faithful records.
translations.idiomatic: Thus our sage ancestors' legacy may rest untarnished and history may transmit no shameful falsehoods.

sentences.zh: 下臣非據，獲減戾於侵官。

translations.literal: Your lowly subject, lacking proper qualification, may reduce the offense of overstepping office.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant, holding office beyond his merits, may thus be spared the charge of overstepping his authority.

sentences.zh: 彰清朝立政之方，表公器不私之義。

translations.literal: Manifesting the clear dynasty's method of establishing government, displaying the public vessel's meaning of not being partial.
translations.idiomatic: This would show how the dynasty governs and uphold the principle that public office must not serve private ends.

sentences.zh: 流言自弭，時論攸宜。

translations.literal: Wandering talk would naturally cease; contemporary opinion would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor would subside of itself, and public opinion would be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「其《實錄》中所書德宗、順宗朝禁中事，尋訪根柢，蓋起謬傳，諒非信史。

translations.literal: Edict said: "In the Veritable Records as written, the inner-palace affairs of the Dezong and Shunzong reigns—tracing to their roots, they largely arose from erroneous transmission; surely they are not trustworthy history.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Tracing the origins of the inner-palace accounts from the reigns of Emperors Dezong and Shunzong recorded in the Veritable Records, we find they stem largely from false rumor and cannot be regarded as reliable history.

sentences.zh: 宜令史官詳正刊去，其他不要更修。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order historians to examine, correct, and delete; other matters need not further revision.
translations.idiomatic: Let the historians examine these passages, correct them, and delete what is unsound; no other portions need be revised.

sentences.zh: 余依所奏。」

translations.literal: The remainder follows what was memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest, follow the memorial."

sentences.zh: 四年，轉門下侍郎，加崇文館大學士。

translations.literal: Fourth year, transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery, added Grand Academician of the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery and made Grand Academician of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 七年，兼太子太師，備禮冊拜。

translations.literal: Seventh year, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, invested with full ceremony and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was concurrently appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in a full ceremonial investiture.

sentences.zh: 表上史官所修憲宗穆宗《實錄》。

translations.literal: Memorialized submitting the historians' compiled Veritable Records of Emperors Xianzong and Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne presenting the historians' completed Veritable Records of Emperors Xianzong and Muzong.

sentences.zh: 八年，辭疾，不得謝。

translations.literal: Eighth year, he cited illness to resign; could not obtain leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he asked to retire on grounds of illness but was not permitted to leave office.

sentences.zh: 會李德裕連貶至袁州長史，隨不署奏狀，始為鄭註所忌。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Deyu was repeatedly demoted to Chief Administrator of Yuanzhou; Sui did not sign the memorial report, and for the first time incurred Zheng Zhu's resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu was repeatedly demoted as far as chief administrator of Yuanzhou, Lu Sui refused to countersign the memorial of dismissal—thereby incurring Zheng Zhu's enmity for the first time.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，拜檢校尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事，兼潤州刺史、鎮海軍節度、浙江西道觀察等使。

translations.literal: Ninth year fourth month, appointed honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Participant in the Chancellery, concurrently Runzhou Prefect, Zhenhai Army Military Commissioner, and Zhejiang West Circuit Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year he was appointed honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Participant in the Chancellery, with concurrent posts as Prefect of Runzhou, Military Governor of Zhenhai, and Commissioner of the Zhejiang West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太和九年七月，遘疾於路，薨於揚子江之中流，年六十。

translations.literal: Seventh month, ninth year of Tahe, stricken with illness on the road, died in midstream of the Yangzi River, age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year of the Tahe reign he fell ill en route and died midstream on the Yangzi River, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 冊贈太保，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed posthumously as Grand Guardian; posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Zhen, "Upright."

sentences.zh: 隨有學行大度，為諫官能直言，在內廷匡益。

translations.literal: Sui had learning, conduct, and magnanimity; as remonstrance official able to speak plainly; within the inner court he corrected and benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui was learned, magnanimous, and forthright as a censor; within the palace he offered steady corrective counsel.

sentences.zh: 自寶歷初為承旨學士，即參大政矣。

translations.literal: From the beginning of the Baoli era as Chief Academician, he then participated in great governance.
translations.idiomatic: From his appointment as chief academician at the start of the Baoli reign he was already involved in major affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 後十五年在相位。

translations.literal: Afterwards fifteen years in the chancellor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: He then held high ministerial rank for fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 宗閔、德裕朋黨交興，攘臂於其間；

translations.literal: Zongmin and Deyu factional cliques alternately arose, shouldering in among them.
translations.idiomatic: As the factions of Li Zongmin and Li Deyu rose in turn, each brandishing power in the struggle,

sentences.zh: 李訓、鄭註始終奸詐，接武於其後。

translations.literal: Li Xun and Zheng Zhu from beginning to end were treacherous and deceitful, following one upon another after them.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Xun and Zheng Zhu, utterly treacherous, followed close behind—

sentences.zh: 而隨藏器韜光，隆汙一致，可謂得君子中庸而常居之也。

translations.literal: Yet Sui hid his talents and subdued his brilliance, treating exaltation and filth alike; this may be called attaining the Mean of the gentleman and constantly dwelling in it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui concealed his brilliance and held himself above the turmoil, treating honor and disgrace alike—a man who truly lived the Confucian Mean.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：衛次公、鄭絪、韋處厚、崔群、路隨等，皆以文學飾身，致位崇極。

translations.literal: The historian says: Wei Cigong, Zheng Xian, Wei Chuhou, Cui Qun, Lu Sui, and others—all by literary learning adorned themselves and reached lofty positions.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Wei Cigong, Zheng Xian, Wei Chuhou, Cui Qun, Lu Sui, and the others all rose to the highest offices through literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 兼之忠讜，垂名簡書，茲實有足多也。

translations.literal: Together with loyal remonstrance, their names hang on bamboo and silk; this truly has much worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Their loyal remonstrance has earned them lasting fame in the histories—a record richly deserving of praise.

sentences.zh: 絪有其位，有其時，懷獨善之謀，晦眾濟之道，左遷非不幸也。

translations.literal: Xian had his position and his time; he harbored the strategy of preserving his own integrity, obscuring the way of benefiting the multitude—demotion was not misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xian held rank at the right moment yet cherished a policy of personal rectitude above public service; his demotion was no misfortune.

sentences.zh: 次公因獻捷之書，輟已成之詔，命也夫。

translations.literal: Cigong, because of submitting a victory memorial, halted an already completed edict—such was fate!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cigong, having submitted a victory report, saw an already drafted edict withdrawn—such was fate.

sentences.zh: 處厚危言切議，振士友之急，稱同列之善，君子哉！

translations.literal: Chuhou spoke perilous words and keen arguments, roused friends in urgent need, praised colleagues' virtues—what a gentleman!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chuhou spoke boldly in perilous times, rallied friends in distress, and praised his colleagues' virtues—a true gentleman!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：衛、鄭、韋、路，兼之博陵。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Wei, Zheng, Wei, Lu—with Cui of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Wei, Zheng, Wei, and Lu, together with Cui of Boling—

sentences.zh: 文學政事，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Literary learning and governmental affairs—for the times they were praised.
translations.idiomatic: men praised in their age for literary talent and statesmanship.
